| SD-53 | **Medusa 2.14.2's workflow engine can leave `completeCartWorkflow` unfinished after it writes the order and before it authorizes the card; Medusa's test runner then waits forever.** Found when #905's Integration Tests job ran 70 minutes and failed: in `digital-order-settlement.spec.ts` one checkout's link step failed with Postgres `column "true" does not exist`, and every later test of that spec timed out at Jest's 240-second hook limit. Traced on a real database with the engine's own files instrumented (private copies, restored afterwards). (1) *The engine.* Every checkpoint the in-memory engine saves passes a race guard (`@medusajs/workflow-engine-inmemory` `utils/workflow-orchestrator-storage.js`, `#preventRaceConditionExecutionIfNecessary`) that throws `SkipStepAlreadyFinishedError` when the stored flow already shows the step finished, and the orchestrator (`@medusajs/orchestration` `transaction/transaction-orchestrator.js`) treats that error as expected: it stops that execution path with no error and no compensation. The steps of a `parallelize` block share one flow object, so a step's own checkpoint can already show it finished. `completeCartWorkflow` runs such a block right after `createOrdersStep` (`createRemoteLinkStep`, `updateCartsStep`, `reserveInventoryStep`, `registerUsageStep`, `emitEventStep`), and on every cart completion logged while this was traced, nested (`runAsStep`) and top-level alike, the guard fired on `register-usage`. That is harmless while another path of the block carries on. When it is not, nothing runs `authorizePaymentSessionStep`: the order, the cart's `order_cart` link and its `completed_at` are written, the card is never authorized, the caller gets no order id, and the `workflow_execution` row stays unfinished (the caller's compensation of it sticks at `waiting_to_compensate`). Seen intermittently: once on CI, and twice in the local Postgres log (the same seller-link insert with no `order_id` and `on conflict ("true")`); a probe hit it once too, possibly one of those two; three dedicated reruns of that probe did not hit it. A step handler that throws the same error stops a run the same way, which is how the specs reproduce it on demand (`integration-tests/http/helpers/stalled-workflows.ts`, `stallNextCartCompletion`: the completion's `order.placed` emit throws it, so the other steps of the block run, as in the race). Whether the Redis engine production runs can stall the same way is unverified: medusa-config wires `workflow-engine-redis` when `REDIS_URL` is set, and its storage has the same guard (read, not run). (2) *What it did to FBM's two checkouts, flag on:* the caller acted on `order_id: undefined`, which a query does not filter on, and a retry delivered the order with no payment at all. Fixed for both, flag on (SD-48 point (17)); with the flags off since (c) was closed (below). (3) *The runner.* `medusaIntegrationTestRunner` (test-utils 2.14.2, `medusa-test-runner-utils/wait-workflow-executions.js`) waits between tests for every execution not `not_started`, `done`, `reverted` or `failed`. Its 60-second timeout throws from a timer callback, which Jest reports against the running test, and its loop never exits, so one unfinished execution made every later hook spin to the hook timeout. The two settlement specs now look for unfinished executions after their subscriber drain, from an `afterEach` registered inside each `describe` block so that it runs before the runner's, mark them failed so the runner's wait ends, and fail the test that left them (`clearStalledWorkflows`). **Open:** (a) report both upstream (Medusa: the guard and `parallelize`; test-utils: the wait that never ends), an operator task; (b) whether `workflow-engine-redis` stalls the same way; (c) flag off, as on `main`, neither checkout is guarded. Seen on a real database for the digital checkout, with another order already in the database: the stalled checkout fails at its order read (`Order: Primary key(s) [id] not found in filters`, Medusa's own `throwIfKeyNotFound`), but a retry runs `completeCartWorkflow` again, finds the order and delivers it with no payment, the digital product order made. Running the paid step whatever the flag says would close it, but changes flag-off behaviour, so it is left for a decision. **Closed 2026-10-12, see below;** (d) every other integration spec that completes a cart can still hit the stall and the runner's endless wait; only the two settlement specs contain it; (e) an order a stall leaves is unpaid and undelivered with its cart completed, so the buyer cannot complete that cart again; an operator has to cancel the order (SD-48 open item (o)); since (c) was closed this holds with the flags off too; (f) the paid check asks only that the order has a payment, and a cancelled one counts. So a stall that follows an earlier attempt on the same cart that failed after the card was authorized (its compensation cancels the payment, and Medusa keeps it on the collection) still lets the retry deliver with that cancelled payment as its only one: seen on a real database with both flags off (the earlier failure a refused digital product order write, then a new payment session) and with `FF_DIGITAL_ORDER_SETTLEMENT_V1` on (the earlier failure a transient read in the link step), the digital product order made and nothing captured. With the flags off, a retry on the same payment session after such a failure is answered with the cancelled payment (`authorizePaymentSession` hands back the payment it has) and delivers as well (seen on a real database; with the flag on the capture step refuses it, SD-48 point (10)). (c) changed neither. Counting only payments that are not cancelled would close both, and would also refuse that flag-off same-session retry, which delivers today: a further flag-off change, so left for a decision. **(c) closed (2026-10-12, branch `-v35`; merged to `main` with #906 on 2026-10-24).** The paid check (`orderPaid`, each checkout's last step before delivery) now runs whatever its sale's flag says. Nothing else changes with the flags off: the seller and capture steps still return before any read, and the subscription checkout still takes no lock. *What it does now, both flags off (real database):* the stalled checkout fails at the paid check ("the cart's completion returned no order"), before its own order read could run on an undefined id; the retry gets the cart's order back from `completeCartWorkflow`, which authorizes nothing on a completed cart, and is refused ("owes money and has no payment"): no digital product order, fulfillment or subscription, no Stripe call, the order and its completed cart left as in (e). Before the change the same scenario on `main` delivered on the retry for both checkouts, the subscription one included (only the digital one had been seen): an active subscription and a digital product order with no payment, Stripe never asked to authorize. Callers now see `UNEXPECTED_STATE` for the stalled checkout instead of the order read's `NOT_FOUND`, and `NOT_ALLOWED` (400 on the store routes) for its retry instead of a delivered order. *Why it changes nothing a flag-off checkout legitimately sold:* both checkouts are reachable with their flags off (`POST /store/subscriptions` has a flag-off branch; Blackout's page completes recurring listings through `createSubscriptionWorkflow` and one-off listings through `create-digital-product-order` whatever either flag says; the digital checkout's three routes are not flag-gated), so before the change every way an order reaches them was run on a real database (a scratch probe, not kept), on `main` and again with the change, both flags off, reading the order at the checkout's read right after the paid check: a card at Stripe over `POST /store/carts/:id/complete-digital`, `/v1/checkout/sessions/:id/page` and `POST /store/subscriptions`; Medusa's system provider; a cart carrying a Coalition Credits reservation (all `POST /store/carts/:id/credits` writes is the ledger reservation and a count in the cart's metadata, so the cart's total and its payment stay the full amount, and CCR has no other checkout path; `docs/POSTURE_A_COMPLIANCE.md`); Blackout's hosted page through its real route, for a one-off and a recurring listing; and Medusa's Stripe webhook completing the cart before the checkout (`processPaymentWorkflow` run directly, with an authorized and with a succeeded intent). Every one had a payment on the order's collection whenever the order owed money, and every one delivered the same with the change. Gift cards and store credit have no checkout path here: no FBM code adds a credit line to a cart, Medusa 2.14.2's only credit-line route is the admin one on an order, and the four store routes tried for them answer 404. An order that owes nothing (a free product with no payment collection, or a free subscription with a session at 0) has no payment and is still delivered: `validateCartPaymentsStep` skips payment for a total of 0 or less. And by construction a first completion that finishes cannot leave an order that owes money without a payment: `authorizePaymentSessionStep` throws unless the session is authorized and the payment module has written the payment. On `main` the second made the subscription at that moment, with no payment on the order; now it is refused, and the first, which by then has its payment, makes the subscription (probed with the first's authorization held back, manual and automatic capture alike: one subscription, nothing refunded or cancelled). By reading, not produced: the refused run's replay of `completeCartWorkflow` registers `compensatePaymentIfNeededStep`, which refunds a captured payment it finds, so with automatic capture (session data a store client can set) a first run whose capture lands while the second is still compensating would be refunded with its subscription made; with the flag off nothing captures these orders otherwise. *Kept as tests:* the unit spec runs the paid check under all four combinations of the two flags for both sales and keeps "returns before any read" for the other steps; each settlement spec runs the stalled checkout and its retry with its own flag off (both flags off, and with the other sale's flag on), a free order delivered, and the flag-off checkouts, over the workflow and the store route, now read as passing through the paid check before anything is delivered. | SD-54 | **Two of the four guards on `completeCartWorkflow`'s `validate` hook never run: the Coalition Credits reservation guard and the order-cycle guard read a cart id the hook does not pass.** Found while listing every way an order reaches FBM's two `completeCartWorkflow` checkouts for SD-53 (c). `workflows/hooks/complete-cart-validate.ts` runs four validators on the hook. Medusa 2.14.2 calls it with `{ input, cart }`, `input` being the workflow's own input, `{ id }` (`@medusajs/core-flows` `cart/workflows/complete-cart.js`: `createHook("validate", { input, cart: cartData.data })`). `validate-sliding-scale-tier.ts` reads `input.id`; `validate-ccr-reservation.ts` and `validate-order-cycle.ts` read `args.input.cart_id`, find nothing, and return before reading the cart. **Seen on a real database** (a scratch probe, not kept): a real `completeCartWorkflow` run on a cart whose metadata held `ccr_credits_reserved: 3` completed into an order, and of the hook's reads of that cart only the sliding-scale guard's happened; FBM's digital-product and subscription checkouts completed such carts too, each with a payment for the full total. `validate-order-cycle.unit.spec.ts` hands the guard `{ input: { cart_id } }` — the shape the code reads, not the one Medusa passes — which is how a green suite hid it; the CCR guard has no test. **What it means, by reading:** (1) with `FBM_CCR_CHECKOUT_LIVE=1` (unset by default), a cart holding a credits reservation completes through any checkout built on `completeCartWorkflow`, at its full total, while the reserved credits stay in the CCR cart escrow against a cart that has completed, neither settled nor released: the double take the guard's own comment says it bolts shut. (2) The order-cycle checks D9-1 and D9-3 record as done — a cycle closed or gone, an item the cycle no longer offers, capacity summed across a cart's lines, all refused before payment — do not run at any checkout. Separately, FBM's main checkout (`POST /store/carts/:id/complete`, which `@mercurjs/b2c-core` serves with `splitAndCompleteCartWorkflow`) never calls this hook, for any of the four guards (read, not run). Not fixed here: outside SD-53's scope, and the fix — read `input.id` as the sliding-scale guard does, and test the hook with the shape Medusa passes — turns two refusals on at checkout, which needs its own review. | fixed: the hook in SD-72, Mercur's main checkout in SD-147 (rental off pending the operator) — **2026-11-15: guards run on `completeCartWorkflow` checkouts (SD-72). 2026-11-17 (merged): the main checkout runs the tier, CCR and order-cycle guards in front of Mercur's route, and answers a cart Medusa's workflow completed with 409 (with its order only when FBM's judge passes it) instead of passing it to Mercur (SD-147). The rental guard stays off it pending the operator. Medusa's generic admin workflow runner can still run Mercur's workflow past them.** | `backend/src/workflows/hooks/complete-cart-validate.ts`, `backend/src/workflows/hooks/validate-ccr-reservation.ts`, `backend/src/workflows/hooks/validate-order-cycle.ts`, `backend/src/workflows/hooks/__tests__/validate-order-cycle.unit.spec.ts` |

| SD-71 | **The 'Report' button on every seller page did nothing: `ReportSellerForm`'s submit handler was `logger.info('Form Data:', data)`, and the view then told the reporter "We'll check ... and take the necessary action", with "Trademark, Copyright or DMCA Violation" as the only reason offered; and the listing-report route it was meant to be built like had never filed an anonymous report either.** Checked at `c1a708e`, not inferred: `storefront/src/components/molecules/ReportSellerForm/ReportSellerForm.tsx:44-46` makes no fetch or SDK call, and `SellerFooter.tsx:44` mounts it in every seller page header. Fix: a new `POST /store/seller-reports`. It needs no session, takes a strict zod body (`seller_id`, a reason from a list of seven, a comment of 10 to 4000 characters, optional `reporter_email`), and requires `seller_id` to resolve through `query.graph`, otherwise 404 and nothing is stored. An accepted report is a `seller_report` row in the request module, so it lands in `GET /admin/requests?type=seller_report`. The reported seller cannot see it, because `/vendor/requests` filters by `submitter_id`. The cap is 10 per hour per IP (`storeReportRateLimiter`). `ReportSellerForm` takes the seller id from `SellerFooter` and sends through `lib/data/seller-reports.ts` (`fileSellerReport`, which never throws). The confirmation appears only on `ok: true`; a failure stays on the form with an error. That module is deliberately not `"use server"`: the cap is IP-keyed, and a server action would put every reporter in the storefront's one bucket (SD-58). Second finding, from building it "like product-reports": `request.submitter_id` is NOT NULL and `createRequest` throws `submitter_id or requester_id is required` when given neither. `POST /store/product-reports` passed only `requester_id`, which is undefined without a session. So every anonymous listing report was a 500, and `ReportListingForm` sends no credentials, so no listing report was ever filed. Observed: the new integration spec's anonymous listing-report case got 500 with that error in the server log. Its unit spec stayed green because it stubbed `createRequest` itself, which is the CLAUDE.md "green suite that proves nothing" case. Both routes now file anonymous reports under `ANONYMOUS_SUBMITTER_ID` (`"anonymous"`; no prefixed actor id can equal it). product-reports gets the same rate limit, because it now accepts anonymous writes for the first time. Independent review (approve, with should-fix items) found that this opened those writes against any `product_id` string, where the seller route required a real seller. product-reports now resolves the product through Query too: an unknown id gets 404 and nothing is stored, and `product_handle` is kept with the report (`7b67c06`, a unit case mutation-checked, and an integration case on Postgres filing against a real product). The task brief assumed product-reports already had a limit; it had none. What proves it: unit specs against both real handlers, running the module's real `createRequest` over a stubbed `createRequests`. A middleware-loader spec shows the 11th report from one IP refused on both routes. An integration spec on real Postgres files against a real mercurjs seller and reads the report back from `/admin/requests`. Vitest covers `fileSellerReport` and the form's submit handler. Eight mutations each made the tests fail, including restoring the original product-reports code (3 unit failures, and the integration 500). medusa build, tsc and lint are green. NOT verified: no browser or e2e run. The form test calls the component with its hooks stubbed, because the storefront's vitest has no DOM library. The browser call relies on the existing STORE_CORS, as `ReportListingForm` already does. Still open: the admin panel has no screen for `seller_report` or `listing_report`; they can only be reached through the `/admin/requests` API. The `request` table is not in `customer-data-registry.ts`: it keys on `customer_id`, and this table uses `submitter_id`/`requester_id`, so a reporter's email in `data` is outside both export and erasure. The schema gap is older, but in practice this change is the first code to write third-party reporter emails into `request.data`, because every browser listing report returned 500 before it. Covering it needs an email-keyed lookup, since an anonymous reporter has no customer id. The success copy still says the report "will be reviewed", and no one is notified when a DMCA notice arrives. `POST /store/requests` and `POST /vendor/requests` accept any `type`, so a customer or seller can insert rows typed `seller_report` with unvalidated data; `submitter_id` identifies them. | SD-79 | **A buyer's claim went nowhere: the admin panel had no screen for order disputes, the claim intake threw on every real order (and, had it not, stored major units floored as minor ones), and `/buyer-protection` promised that a person reads every claim.** Claims filed from the storefront become `order_dispute` rows worked through `GET/PATCH /admin/disputes`, but nothing called those routes. **First pass (5dde6d2, 3b8ad88, aad1556, 1a8cd5d, 8518f1d):** a Disputes queue and case file in the admin panel; the intake asked `query.graph` for `items.total` without a top-level `total` (so every read threw) and for a `product.seller_id` that does not exist, and stored `floor(major total)` in a minor-unit column ($25.99 as 25, shown as $0.25), all fixed and proven on a real database; decisions write only if the status is unchanged (409 otherwise); `scripts/fix-order-dispute-minor-units.ts` to correct old rows; the case file shows what the buyer submitted; the storefront stopped promising attachments and replies. **Review 3 (changes_required, five should-fix items), fixed in 7b8ffd2, 5da5fae, 784d0f1, 4e15337, c41bb1a:** (1) The note field said "not sent to anyone", but the buyer reads it as `reviewer_note` (`GET /store/order-claims`) and `resolution_note` (`GET /store/orders/:id/dispute`) and the seller in `GET /vendor/disputes/:id`; relabelled "the buyer and the seller can read this in their claim records; it is not emailed". (2) The corrective script judged rows on their amounts alone. 3b8ad88's reasoning ("a claim above the old figure was stored after the fix; anything else is reviewed") was wrong for the equal case: since the fix a buyer can type `claim_amount` 25 on a $25.99 order through `POST /store/orders/:id/dispute`, which is exactly an old row, and a late run would have made it $25.99 along with a whole-claim award. Now `OrderDisputeService.open` stamps `metadata.amount_unit = "minor"` in the same insert (the intake's metadata is no longer a second write) and the planner skips stamped rows; the script requires `before=<ISO time with a zone>`, filters `created_at < before` and checks it again in the planner, and refuses no, zone-less or future cutoffs; the store route answers a non-integer `claim_amount` with 400 `invalid_claim_amount` and documents it as minor units. Found doing it, checked against the real CLI on a migrated database: `medusa exec` parses with yargs in strict mode, so `--dry-run`/`--before=` are refused as unknown arguments and anything after `--` is dropped before the script sees it. 3b8ad88's documented `--dry-run` never ran, and `-- --dry-run` would have been a live run; the script takes bare words now and refuses to run with none. (3) Step 3 now says the claim goes into a review queue (nothing notifies an operator on intake). `PATCH /admin/disputes/:id` refuses refund, release or withdrawal without a non-empty note (400 `note_required`, `DECISIONS_NEEDING_A_NOTE`), which only the panel enforced before, and `buyer-protection-copy.spec.ts` allows "written reason" only while that check is in the route. (4) `scripts/backfill-order-claims.ts` runs the same intake, so every run before 3b8ad88 failed every row and left legacy claims pending in `request`. No logic bug: a real-database case shows the re-run moves a pending claim and its `legacy_request_id` lookup works (a moved claim left pending is skipped while a fresh one moves). Two small fixes: its reviewer note no longer hard-codes "on 2026-09-03", and the logger key is imported. (5) The screens had never rendered (no DOM test library). `e2e/tests/admin-disputes.spec.ts` drives them in Chromium with every `/admin/*` call mocked by `page.route`. It found three bugs, now fixed: the decision PATCH was sent twice on a 409 (the app-wide mutation default retries once; `retry: false` now), the case file kept offering a decision after a 409 (it now refetches on settle), and decided rows showed days waiting. **Proven:** backend unit 92/92 across 8 suites (5 new or changed); `admin-disputes.spec.ts` 13/13 on Postgres for the backend source as committed; on the committed tree itself two runs gave 12/13 and 10/13, every failure being the runner's between-test `TRUNCATE` hitting "out of shared memory" on the shared server, and each case passed in at least one of the two; admin-panel vitest 37/37; storefront vitest 663/663; the e2e spec 4/4 against `vite` dev and against a production build with CI's baked backend URL. Each guard added here was mutation-checked: removing it fails at least one test. **Deploy note:** (a) Write down when this branch goes live. (b) `npx medusa exec ./src/scripts/fix-order-dispute-minor-units.ts dry-run before=<that time, e.g. 2026-11-20T15:00:00Z>`, read the corrected/skipped/review lines, then run it again without `dry-run`. Rows listed for review are left for a person. (c) `npx medusa exec ./src/scripts/backfill-order-claims.ts` (idempotent by `legacy_request_id`) and check `moved`/`failed`. A failure logged as `ambiguous_vendor` is a legacy claim on an order with more than one seller (the old form never named one) and has to be filed by hand. **Still open:** nothing notifies an operator when a claim arrives; no page shows a buyer the outcome (`listOrderClaims` has no caller) and nothing emails it; no vendor-panel screen for the seller's reply; the PATCH reads a non-number `award_amount` (for example the string "12.50") as no amount and awards the whole claim (the panel always sends an integer; found, not fixed); the same `medusa exec` argument handling breaks `reencrypt-channel-credentials.ts` (documents `-- --apply`, which never reaches it, so it can never apply) and `backfill-promoted-listings.ts` (documents `--dry-run`, which the CLI refuses) (found, not fixed); the panel-wide retry-once default still applies to every other mutation; the e2e spec has not been watched in the e2e workflow yet. | fixed (`5dde6d2` … `c41bb1a` on `claude/intelligent-mayer-7zymwu`, from `fix/p0-admin-disputes-screen`; it also fixed the dispute intake's `items.total` read, so SD-52's ratchet entry for `shared/order-dispute-intake.ts` came out); e2e spec not yet watched in CI; operator notification, buyer-facing outcome and vendor reply screen open — follow-up fixes: SD-80. | `admin-panel/src/routes/disputes/**`, `admin-panel/src/hooks/api/disputes.tsx`, `backend/src/modules/order-dispute/**`, `backend/src/shared/order-dispute-intake.ts`, `backend/src/api/admin/disputes/[id]/route.ts`, `backend/src/api/store/orders/[id]/dispute/route.ts`, `backend/src/scripts/{fix-order-dispute-minor-units,backfill-order-claims}.ts`, `backend/integration-tests/http/admin-disputes.spec.ts`, `storefront/src/app/[locale]/(main)/buyer-protection/page.tsx`, `e2e/tests/admin-disputes.spec.ts` |
| SD-80 | **The re-review of the admin disputes fixes (two refuters each) left five should-fix defects, all real when re-checked against the code: the PATCH turned any non-number `award_amount` into a whole-claim refund, the corrective script wrote unless it saw exactly `dry-run`, both vendor dispute routes gave every vendor an empty list or a 404, "Back to disputes" showed a decided case as Open from cache, and the e2e 409 test pinned a message the backend does not send for that case.** (1) *Award.* `awardCents: typeof body.award_amount === "number" ? … : null` read "0", "12.50", `true` and `[1250]` as no figure, so the whole claim was paid. `resolveAwardCents` turned -500 into a refund of 0 and rounded 12.5 down. The route now accepts only absent, null or a whole number of zero or more (`parseAwardAmount`). Anything else gets 400 `invalid_award_amount` before anything is read or written. `resolveAwardCents` throws `DisputeAwardError` (a subclass of `DisputeStateError`) for a malformed award, an award over the claim, money on a release, and a refund of nothing; a refund of nothing is told to use `resolved_release`, and the panel's `resolutionDraft` refuses it too. The route answers `DisputeAwardError` with 400. Over-claim and award-on-release therefore moved from 409 to 400, and a 409 now means only that the case moved on. (2) *Corrective script.* A mistyped `dryrun`, `dry_run` or `DRY-RUN` with a valid cutoff ran live, unknown words were ignored, a second `before=` lost to the first, and `2026-02-30` became 2026-03-02. Writing is now opt-in: it needs `apply`, and no word is a dry run, as is `fixOrderDisputeMinorUnits` without `apply: true`. Any other word, a repeated word or `before=`, and `apply` with `dry-run` are refused by name. A cutoff whose typed date and time do not read back unchanged in its zone is refused. The write is one conditional UPDATE on the planned status, claim and award, which also refuses a marked or already-corrected row (`OrderDisputeService.correctAmountsIfUnchanged`). A row that changed is listed for review. Skipped rows are logged with their reason. A correction to a decided refund is flagged ("check the Stripe refund matches") in the log line, the event and `amount_units_corrected.refund_check`. Pages are ordered by `created_at`, then `id`. (3) *Vendor routes.* Both took the seller from `auth_context.actor_id`, which for a vendor login is the member id (SD-74's finding). So the operator copy saying the seller reads the note and can reply was false. They now find the seller with `requireSellerId` and return a limited vendor view (`order-dispute/views.ts`): no customer or admin ids, no escrow id, no metadata, no event actor ids. A reply to a missing dispute is now 404, the same as another vendor's. Nit: `GET /store/orders/:id/dispute` and its POST response return a limited buyer view instead of raw rows that carried `resolved_by` and metadata. (4) *Stale queue.* `onSettled` invalidated the lists with the default `refetchType: "active"`, the queue is unmounted on the case-file route, and `lib/query-client.ts` sets `refetchOnMount: false`. `useDisputes` and `useDispute` now refetch on every mount (`"always"`), and the lists are invalidated with `refetchType: "all"`. (5) *409.* For an already-decided case the backend says "cannot move a dispute from resolved_release to resolved_refund", now pinned on Postgres. The mock sends that, a separate test sends the race message through `raceNext`, and `decisionErrorText` turns any 409 into "This dispute was already decided or changed by someone else. The page now shows where it stands." Nits also done: "Marks it as yours" now says taking a case up assigns nothing. Storefront step 4 no longer offers a replacement or an explanation the buyer cannot receive, and `buyer-protection-copy.spec.ts` refuses both. *Proof.* Each fix was mutation-checked: reverted, watched fail, restored. Route award check reverted: 12 unit cases fail. Old `resolveAwardCents`: 7 fail. Unknown words ignored and opt-out restored: 5 fail. Rollover check removed: 2 fail. The old unconditional write: the new Postgres case fails because the decided refund is overwritten. Vendor routes back on `actor_id`: `vendor-disputes.spec.ts` 2 of 3 fail with 404. Hooks and 409 mapping reverted: 4 of 7 e2e cases fail in Chromium (no toast; 2 rows, not 1; stale form). Store GET on raw rows: 1 fails. Old step-4 copy: 2 fail. Panel refund-of-nothing rule removed: 1 fails. Green: backend dispute and source-scanning unit specs 376/376 in 14 suites; `admin-disputes.spec.ts` 15/15 and `vendor-disputes.spec.ts` 3/3 on Postgres 16; admin-panel vitest 42/42; storefront copy spec 6/6; e2e 7/7 against a production build with CI's baked backend URL (`vite preview`); `medusa build` then `tsc --noEmit` clean (tsc needed `--max-old-space-size=6144` locally); eslint clean on every changed file; admin-panel and storefront `tsc` clean. **Deploy note (replaces SD-79's (b)):** the dry run, which writes nothing, is `npx medusa exec ./src/scripts/fix-order-dispute-minor-units.ts before=<go-live time, e.g. 2026-11-20T15:00:00Z>`. Read the would-correct, skipped and review lines; refund corrections say "check the Stripe refund matches". Then run `npx medusa exec ./src/scripts/fix-order-dispute-minor-units.ts apply before=<same time>`, ideally before anyone works the queue. Rows decided in between are listed for review, not written. **References corrected:** SD-79's first-pass hashes 9386b23, c530777, a94b2b6, a29686c and 7953ce7 are 5dde6d2, 3b8ad88, aad1556, 1a8cd5d and 8518f1d on `claude/intelligent-mayer-7zymwu`. Review 3's fb4b3d5, 85d4a58, 30c598c, 34521fe and d6c1d8f are 7b8ffd2, 5da5fae, 784d0f1, 4e15337 and c41bb1a. Matched one-to-one by commit subject; `fix/p0-admin-disputes-screen` was never on origin. **Not verified / still open:** the vendor panel has no disputes screen (`vendor-panel/src` has no route, hook or call for `/vendor/disputes`), and no storefront page shows the buyer the note. So "the buyer and the seller can read this" is true of the APIs only. The vendor view leaves out the buyer's evidence links and `contacted_seller`; whether the respondent should see them is the operator's call. Classes now get one reminder per start time, claimed by a stamp (`metadata.class_reminder`) written in one conditional UPDATE. A run that reached nobody releases the claim, and a rescheduled class is reminded again. The 24h booking reminder had the same spam and its table has no column to stamp, so it now uses the window [now+23h, now+24h). A missed run therefore skips that hour's bookings rather than re-sending. The update takes a field allow-list. The embed route and `GET /store/vendors/:handle/availability` check that the product belongs to the key's or handle's seller before reading that seller's config. The subscriber confirms only when the order has a line for the booking's product, the product is the booking seller's (Mercur `seller_product`), and the order's seller link, when present, agrees. That also stops a multi-seller cart's other split orders, which all recover the cart's `booking_id`, from confirming it; before, the last to run won. The reminder reads the booking seller's own config zone. Existing foreign rows are ignored on every read. Because of the constraint they cannot be ignored on write, so the owner's save (`saveConfigAsProductOwner`) takes the row over, resets every field and logs the previous seller. **Proven** in `integration-tests/http/booking-seller-scope.spec.ts` (10 cases, real Postgres); `wellness-seller-scope.spec.ts` (15) still passes. *Mutation-checked*, each failing its own cases at the expected assertion. The race loser is refused while only authorized: capture 0, refund 0, hold cancelled. A refused capture deletes the purchases through their compensation and frees the seat. (3) 67f5e372: the order refetch runs before the capture, so the capture is the last step that can fail. | SD-96 | **Creator commission is now converted to minor units where Medusa's major-unit subtotal enters. A real $25 order at 10% records 250 on Postgres, the payout breakdown pays the creator 250 and the vendor the rest, and the ledger credits and a refund reverses $2.50. The corrective script lists, rather than corrects, the orders where it can see that correcting would set up a vendor debit nobody decided on; the third review found two cases it cannot yet see (below). The same work found that no creator commission has ever been credited.** *Premise, verified on Postgres:* through the live checkout (an affiliate click, `POST /store/carts/:id/attribution`, then `POST /store/carts/:id/complete` running Mercur's split-and-complete, with the app's own `order.placed` subscribers), Medusa 2.14.2's `query.graph` returns `subtotal` 25 for $25.00. The old conversion stored subtotal/basis 25 and commission 2, and the stored breakdown gave the creator 2 and the vendor a net of 2423. Every reader traced reads the column as cents and none compensated: payout-breakdown, approve-held via `creditCreatorCommission`, the refund reversal via `reverseCreatorCommission`, both rollups, `/v1/seller/creator/earnings`, `/vendor/analytics/creator`, Blackout `referral.attributed`, the webhooks, the vendor-panel Commission card, creator studio and the admin creators screen. *Fix (`674cf4d`, `09eaa0c3` here):* `subscribers/attribute-order-on-placed.ts` converts with `toMinorUnits(order.subtotal ?? order.total, currency_code)`, which takes each currency's minor-unit digits from Intl (USD 2, JPY 0, KWD 3). The helper moved to `shared/minor-units.ts` and is re-exported from `order-dispute/resolution.ts`. The subscriber marks its rows `metadata.amount_unit = "minor"`. `attributeOrder` refuses a non-positive or fractional `subtotalCents`: it catches $25.50 passed as 25.5, not $25 passed as 25. No reader and no column meaning changed. *Existing rows:* `scripts/fix-creator-commission-minor-units.ts`, a dry run unless given `apply`. It is an operator script, not a migration, because credited rows need a person's decision and a migration would race a rolling deploy's old instances. The planner (`creator-attribution/minor-unit-correction.ts`) corrects an order's chain only when no row is marked, the stored figures equal the old formula on the order's current subtotal at every level, and no row has moved money to the creator. *Review follow-up (`654c094`, `21529a1`; `fec35f30`, `3451fbfb` here):* (a) A held row's commission was never taken from the vendor either. Settlement credits SELLER_EARNINGS the sale less fee and processing, and approve-held later debits `vendor_id` at whatever the column says. So correcting a held row raises that future debit 100x, out of the vendor's balance at the time. The script now lists an order for review instead of correcting it when a row approve-held will still credit names a vendor who is not the order's seller (or the order has no seller), or a vendor paid out since the order was placed (a `hawala_payout_request` PROCESSING, IN_TRANSIT or COMPLETED created after it, or a completed WITHDRAWAL or VENDOR_PAYMENT leg off their SELLER_EARNINGS), or when a Mercur payout (`order.payouts`) already sent the order's proceeds. The check is `reviewVendorDebit`. The header, the README row and a dry-run warning say what `apply` sets up. (b) Corrected rows are also marked `amount_unit = "minor"`. (c) Each order's chain is written in one transaction by `CreatorAttributionService.correctAttributionAmountsIfUnchanged`: per row, one `UPDATE … WHERE id, commission_status and the three planned amounts match, and the row is unmarked and uncorrected, RETURNING id`, with the bigNumber `raw_*` columns written from the same value. A row that changed rolls the chain back and is listed; this was a list-then-update per row. *Proof:* `integration-tests/http/creator-commission-minor-units.spec.ts` passes 4/4 on Postgres 16. (1) The live order case. (2) The script case: the dry run writes nothing; apply corrects a held old-unit row to 2500/250, with raw JSONB identical to an ORM-written 2500/250 row, and leaves a credited row and a marked row alone; a second run skips. (3) The vendor-check case: vendors paid after the order by a COMPLETED payout request, a WITHDRAWAL leg or a VENDOR_PAYMENT leg, and a link vendor that did not sell the order, are listed and left untouched; a vendor paid only before the order, plus a FAILED request after it, is corrected. (4) The chain case: L2 planned from a stale status rolls back L1. The operator SQL below runs verbatim in the spec. Mutations, each red and then restored: conversion reverted (stored 25 where 2500 was expected); vendor check disabled; no mark plus the old SQL (1), which lists the corrected and later correctly credited row (the double payment the review predicted); one transaction per row (L1 committed while L2 was refused); status condition dropped from the UPDATE (a stale write accepted). Both typecheckers and lint are green. **New finding, not fixed here (now SD-99): no creator commission is ever credited.** Where card settlement under `FF_CARD_ORDER_LEDGER_V1` opened the vendor's SELLER_EARNINGS in the ledger default "USD", approve-held opens the creator's CREATOR_EARNINGS in the attribution's lowercase "usd", and `createTransfer`'s exact-match cross-rail guard refuses the transfer ("debit account is USD, credit account is usd"). Verified on Postgres. With the flag off, legacy settlement throws (SD-39), the vendor has no account, `getOrCreateSellerEarnings(vendor, "usd")` opens a zero-balance lowercase one, and the transfer fails on insufficient balance instead (read from code, not run). Either way the row stays held and is retried hourly. Failed attempts leave lowercase CREATOR_EARNINGS accounts and possibly lowercase SELLER_EARNINGS ones, and a later card settlement for such a vendor would itself hit the guard (inferred). The repair must normalise the code without loosening the guard, which is also what keeps USD commission out of a creator's CCR wallet (creator-hub opens CREATOR_EARNINGS in CCR, and `getOrCreateCreatorEarnings` matches on type and owner only). It must also relabel both kinds of zero-balance lowercase account. The probable consequence: vendors kept the whole commission and it went out in their payouts. Posture A: no CCR path is involved; commission is in the order's currency and its legs carry `reference_type` CREATOR_ATTRIBUTION. **Open, pre-existing, made 100x larger by this fix (now SD-100; fix (1) before the cross-rail repair lets commission move):** (1) `attributeOrder` takes `vendor_id` from the link or promo binding, never from the order. Under split-and-complete every order in the cart carries the link's vendor, as does any later order from another seller inside the cookie window. All are fixed.** (a) `Migration20261115210000AddUniqueBallotIndex` (merged in #917, possibly run; not edited) recomputes every proposal that had a duplicate ballot, whatever its status, and keeps no copy of the tally. Each is logged at warn with status, `approval_percentage`, `quorum_met`, when its result was calculated ("before the rewrite" or "after the rewrite", against the removed ballots' `deleted_at`), how many duplicates were removed and when, the tally as it stands and the approval that tally gives (for / (for + against), abstentions left out, as finalize computes it); the message says the earlier tally is gone and `approval_percentage` and `quorum_met` are the only trace. Each is also marked: `metadata.tally_rewritten_by` (the index migration), `tally_rewritten_at`, `tally_rewrite_recorded_by` (the repair). The mark writes `metadata` only (tally, status, result fields and `updated_at` unchanged), so it cannot change a decision. Read it by the two timestamps: `result_calculated_at` before `duplicates_removed_at` means the proposal was decided on a tally that no longer exists; after it, on the recomputed tally, unless the gap is moments (a finalize in flight while the migration ran; the result's time is the app server's clock, the removal's the database's). | SD-105 | **The sales report's CSV export now writes its Date column and its file name in the vendor's time zone, sent as a validated `time_zone` parameter; before, an export for a Los Angeles day held that day's evening orders dated the next day.** Checked in code at `3451fbf` before changing anything, and reproduced, not inferred: `route.ts` wrote the Date cell as `new Date(item.order_date).toISOString().split("T")[0]` and built the Content-Disposition name from the UTC dates of the window's ends, in both CSV branches. The extended integration case failed against that route (expected `sales-report-2025-11-13-to-2025-11-13.csv`, got `…-to-2025-11-14.csv`). *Fix:* `GET /vendor/sales-report` takes an optional `time_zone`, an IANA zone name. A new `sales-report/time-zone.ts` requires a string (a zone name ICU knows: IANA names and their aliases, see the review below), checks its shape (segments of letters, digits, `_`, `+`, `-`, starting with a letter), then builds an `Intl.DateTimeFormat` with it, which throws for a zone it does not know. The shape check is there because Intl on Node 22.23 also accepts UTC offsets (`-08:00`, `+0530`; probed), and an offset is not a zone and is wrong across a DST change. Anything else is a 400 `invalid_data` that does not repeat the value, for JSON and CSV alike, checked after `requireSellerId`. The validated name is only handed to Intl: dates are formatted in JS with `formatToParts` (Gregorian calendar and Latin digits pinned), and the name reaches neither SQL nor a header. With a zone, the Date column and the file name in both branches are that zone's dates; without one (absent or empty) they are UTC dates through the same expression as before, so other callers are unchanged. The zone changes how a date is written, never which orders are counted. The panel's `salesReportQuery` adds the browser's zone, so the JSON request and the CSV export both carry it; a browser that reports `Etc/Unknown` (which the backend refuses) or no zone sends none. **The JSON response needs no change and has none:** `order_date` is the instant and the panel formats it in the browser's zone. That is pinned on both sides: the integration case shows the JSON identical with and without `time_zone`, and a panel case shows a 03:30Z order rendering as the previous local day. *Proof:* `time-zone.unit.spec.ts` (63 cases) covers US zones, links, three-segment names, both 2026 DST changes, offsets, unknown zones, SQL-, header-, path- and template-shaped strings and non-strings; it also passes under `TZ=America/Los_Angeles` and `TZ=Asia/Tokyo`. `vendor-sales-analytics.spec.ts` on Postgres, extended inside its third case so the file still spends 18 of `/auth`'s 20 POSTs: a 19:30 PST order on 2025-11-13 (03:30Z on the 14th) is `"2025-11-14"` in `sales-report-2025-11-13-to-2025-11-14.csv` without a zone, and `"2025-11-13"` in `sales-report-2025-11-13-to-2025-11-13.csv` with `America/Los_Angeles`, the rest of the row byte-identical. It also checks the no-products branch, a two-day range, `Asia/Tokyo`, and 400s for five bad zones on both formats. 5/5 pass. Mutations of the route each fail on Postgres: Date cell back to UTC; either branch's file name back to UTC; a bad zone falling back to UTC (400 expected, 200 received). Mutations of the validator fail in the unit spec: no shape check 3, no string check 2, unknown zone not refused 9, zone ignored 22. `sales-report.spec.tsx`, still under `TZ=America/Los_Angeles`, checks the zone on the JSON request and on the request the real Export CSV button makes: 12/12; with the zone never sent 6 fail, without the `Etc/Unknown` guard 1, with the zone dropped from the CSV request only 1. `medusa build`, then `tsc --noEmit` (6 GB heap): 0 errors. Lint on the touched backend files passes. Panel `typecheck`, `lint` and the full suite (142) pass; the page, hook and spec, which are outside the panel's `typecheck` project, have 0 errors under a scratch strict tsconfig. **Not verified / open:** the panel was not opened in a browser, and CI was not watched. The two assertions added after the mutation runs (the default panel query's `time_zone` and that export's file name) run in a UTC process, where they cannot tell zone dates from UTC dates. The JSON request now carries the zone too, so a browser zone the server's ICU does not know (tzdata newer than Node's) would turn the whole report into a 400, not only the export; none was observed. A date-only bound stays a UTC day even with `time_zone`. The CSV does not say which zone its Date column is in. "The vendor's zone" is still the browser's; no stored seller zone exists. **Independent review: approve, three nits, none changed.** (1) The JSON request carries the zone too, so a browser zone the server's ICU does not know turns the whole page into a 400, not only the export; probed under 19 odd `TZ` settings, the browser's reported zone was always a name the validator accepts, `Etc/Unknown` or undefined, and the panel sends none for the last two. (2) The validator also accepts ICU's legacy ids that are not IANA names (`PST`, `CST`, `IST`, `ACT`, `SystemV/AST4ADT`); they map to real zones and the output is still digits and hyphens, so it is a wording gap, not a safety one, and no test pins it. (3) `time_zone` with date-only bounds names the file outside the dates typed (`start_date=2025-11-13&end_date=2025-11-13&time_zone=America/Los_Angeles` gives `sales-report-2025-11-12-to-2025-11-13.csv`); the panel never sends that combination and no test pins it. The list returns the caller's own batches, or the runs of a courier they own (the two principals the batch read serves), and refuses a caller with no account. A seller's page therefore lists only those of the seller's products that fall in that page, and the category, type, sales-channel, size and price facets work within one page. The seller page was checked on a two-product catalogue only. Needs a backend filter by seller. If a seller's first eight published products are all outside the channel or unpriced, the section shows fewer than four. (6) Prices display tax-inclusive where the tax module has a default rate for the country (review measured 5.50 and 44 for the $5 and $40 variants with a 10% rate on `us`); whether that is the intended display for US shoppers is undecided. | SD-115 | **Mercur's shipping-method routes and FBM's tier and wholesale routes change a cart's total without refreshing its payment collection, so a card session is opened, or left pending, for an amount that is not the cart's total; the storefront's own delivery step reaches this on any multi-seller cart whose buyer picks, changes or removes a shipping method after a payment collection exists.** *Reach, measured by the second review of SD-114* on Postgres 16 through the real store routes with only Stripe's API stubbed; state was read from the database, because the routes answer 500 on their response read after the write (SD-117). Scenario 1, a buyer edits delivery after choosing the card: two sellers, items 10 + 10, shipping 5 and 7; cart total 32, card session 32, intent created for 3200. `POST /store/carts/:id/shipping-methods` with the second seller's other option (9): cart total 34, `payment_collection.amount` 29, no sessions. Opening the card session again (the SDK's two calls): session 29, intent 2900, cart still 34. Scenario 2, a buyer reaches payment, goes back and adds another seller's item: one seller, total 15, session 15; `POST /store/carts/:id/line-items` for the other seller's variant, total 25, collection 25 (Medusa's route keeps them together); picking that seller's shipping (7), total 32, collection 27, new session 27, intent 2700. Removing a method: `DELETE /store/carts/:id/shipping-methods` for one seller's method, total 29, collection still 34, the pending 34 session survives. Cure: `refreshPaymentCollectionForCartWorkflow` on the scenario 1 cart gives collection 34, the session deleted, the next session 34 and its intent 3400. Cause, read in `@mercurjs/b2c-core` 1.5.0: `addSellerShippingMethodToCartWorkflow` runs Medusa's `addShippingMethodToCartWorkflow`, which replaces every method and refreshes the collection to items plus the new option, then re-adds the other sellers' methods with the bare `addShippingMethodToCartStep` and nothing after it; `removeCartShippingMethodsWorkflow` is the bare remove step. Storefront callers: `setShippingMethod` (`CartShippingMethodsSection.tsx`) and `removeShippingMethod` (`CartShippingMethodRow.tsx`); the delivery section shows an Edit button once it is done. A first straight pass is not affected: no collection exists until the payment step, and it is then created at the full total. By that review's reading only: Mercur's `split-and-complete-cart` authorizes the first pending session with no amount check and records each order's authorized amount from the order total, so a direct API caller can complete a cart on a session smaller than its total. *The tier and wholesale routes, as first written up in the first review of SD-114,* which is what makes it matter: until that fix no card session could be opened from the storefront. *Measured by the review* through the real tier route on a booted backend (Postgres 16, only Stripe's API stubbed): a cart at 20.00 with a card session (intent created for 2000); `POST /store/carts/:id/tier {tier:"solidarity"}` answered 200 with `line_items_repriced: 1`; afterwards the cart total was 13, the payment collection amount still 20, the same pending `pp_stripe_stripe` session still held the same intent at 2000, and Stripe `update` and `cancel` were never called. *Reproduced here in a committed spec* with the cart-module write both routes make (`cartModule.updateLineItems`, `tier/route.ts:285`, `wholesale/route.ts:366`): a 59.97 cart repriced to 38.97 keeps a 59.97 collection and a pending 59.97 session on the same intent, with no Stripe call; opening the session again creates another intent for 5997, because `createPaymentSessionsWorkflow` takes the collection's amount and the store route returns the existing collection as it is; `refreshPaymentCollectionForCartWorkflow` then re-amounts the collection to 38.97, deletes the session and cancels the intent, and a new session is for 3897. *By reading only:* neither route runs a workflow after the write, and nothing under `backend/src` calls `refreshPaymentCollectionForCartWorkflow` or `refreshCartItemsWorkflow`; `quotes/[id]/accept/route.ts:237` reprices the same way but on a cart it has just created, which has no collection yet; Mercur's `split-and-complete-cart` checks only that a pending session exists before authorizing it and its `order-set-placed-payment-capture` subscriber captures (the review's reading, not re-read here); the tier widget renders only when `item.product.seller.playbook` or `.metadata.playbook` is set and Mercur's Seller model has neither, and the wholesale route has no storefront caller, so the storefront UI does not reach the tier and wholesale routes today and a direct API call does; the shipping-method routes above it does reach. **Interim, merged (`ab68ec8a`):** the storefront's pay button refuses to confirm a card session whose amount is not the cart's total and says the card was not charged. That is all it does. It sees only the cart the page rendered, so a page rendered before the reprice and any caller of the store API are not stopped; and the buyer cannot recover, because choosing the card again opens a session at the same stale amount. **Fix in progress:** refresh the payment collection after Mercur's POST and DELETE shipping-method routes and after the tier and wholesale writes, and reword the pay button's notice. As first written up: the two routes should refresh the payment side after repricing, with a real-database spec asserting that no pending session survives a change of total. Decide which workflow: `refreshPaymentCollectionForCartWorkflow` is the one shown to clear it; `refreshCartItemsWorkflow` also recomputes taxes and promotion adjustments, which a module-level reprice may equally leave stale (not checked). A check at completion that the session's amount equals the cart's total would close the stale-page and direct-API cases as well; none exists. | SD-125 | **The SD-95 corrective script no longer leaves any debit of the vendor's earnings out by its label or its status, and lists an order that already has a ledger entry under the key approve-held credits its row with; another order's creator commission is now listed too, not corrected; "dry run only" stands.** *Re-run before anything changed.* At `6f16fa28`, on orders placed through the real checkout, with the script untouched (`6ab693e6`), a dry run would correct: (B) $20 off the vendor's SELLER_EARNINGS through `POST /admin/hawala/transfers` with `entry_type` CREATOR_COMMISSION; (B2) the same with `reference_type` CREATOR_ATTRIBUTION and a reference id; (D) the order's own commission credited at the old figure with its row still held; and two orders with a PENDING leg off the vendor's earnings. *How the leg is posted (read).* `creditCreatorCommission` calls `createTransfer` with entry type CREATOR_COMMISSION, reference type CREATOR_ATTRIBUTION, the attribution row as reference id, the order id and the key `creator-commission-<row id>`, off the vendor's SELLER_EARNINGS into the creator's CREATOR_EARNINGS. One entry carries both sides. Every one of those is a label `createTransfer` takes from its caller. The admin route forwards entry type, reference type, reference id, idempotency key and metadata, and not the order id (pinned on Postgres: an `order_id` sent in the body is dropped). *Decision 1: no entry type is left out.* The gate lists an order when money has left the earnings its commission would be debited from. Leaving out "another order's commission" rests on two things the script does not read: that the leg is one, and that the other order's own proceeds were in the same earnings, without which its commission came out of another sale, possibly this one. So it is listed, and the line names the other order. The review's narrower filter was run as a mutation and lists B, B2 and D; it differs only in correcting that order. It should cost nothing where the script is meant to run, since SD-99 says no commission is credited today; that is an inference, not checked on production. *Decision 2: no status is asked for.* `createTransfer` is the only writer of ledger entries (grep). It writes the leg PENDING, moves both balances in one database transaction, then marks the leg COMPLETED in a separate statement, so a PENDING leg may have moved money. Run on Postgres: with that last statement failing, the admin route answered 400, the $20 had left the vendor's earnings and the leg stayed PENDING. REVERSED moved money before a refund relabelled it. FAILED is rolled back whole in a database transaction, but the ledger's fallback (`applyBalancePairWithCompensation`) can leave the debit applied, so it counts too. A leg that is COMPLETED or SETTLED is worded as money taken; any other as a debit the ledger cannot vouch for. *Decision 3: commission already taken.* The script reads, by key and in any status, whatever sits under `creator-commission-<row id>` for each of the order's rows, and lists the order. `createTransfer` returns whatever exists under a key before it looks at anything else, so that entry is what approve-held is handed back. The only legs left out of the debit read are left out by id, and each is one the order is already listed for. *Found on the way, run on Postgres, not fixed here (approve-held was out of scope).* approve-held approves a row on whatever entry it is handed back, without looking at its status. (a) Its own credit failing at the balance move leaves a FAILED entry under the key; the next run approved the row with that entry, the vendor's balance unchanged and the creator's zero. (b) An entry an admin posts under the key through the manual-transfer route, out of another seller's earnings, is approved on the same way. The designated-return path already refuses a PENDING or FAILED entry handed back to it; `creditCreatorCommission` does not. This belongs with the SD-99 repair. *Proof.* `creator-commission-minor-units.spec.ts` 17/17 on Postgres 16 (was 14). New, on orders placed through the real checkout: B, B2 and another order's commission each listed for that one leg; the order's own commission made by the approve-held job itself with its row update lost, an entry posted by hand under the key, and a FAILED credit, each listed for the entry under its key and nothing else, after which the job approves each row at the old figure; two PENDING legs; a corrected control in each case. Unit: 53 in the two specs (was 50). Mutations, each red then restored with checksums compared: 8 on Postgres (the fix reverted; the entry-type exclusion back; the status filter back; the key read dropped; the review's narrower filter; a wrong key; the gate ignoring commission entries; the gate ignoring unconfirmed legs) and 19 in unit. `medusa build`, then `tsc --noEmit` (0 errors, 6 GB heap; a type error planted in all three spec files was reported, then removed), eslint on the changed `src` files and `check-no-console` green. Posture A: reads only; no ledger write, entry type, reference type or CCR path; `test:posture-a` 58 passed. `lib/card-order-reconcile.ts`, `lib/card-order-settlement.ts`, the unit fix and approve-held untouched. **Not verified:** CI; the script against a production copy; this change has had no review. The lost row update, the failed balance move and the failed COMPLETED update are each produced by making that one call throw in the spec, not by a process dying. The job's credits in those cases get through only because the spec opens the creator's account as "USD"; SD-99 (1) refuses them otherwise. Events ran on the local bus, not Redis. That no CREATOR_COMMISSION leg exists in production today is inferred from SD-99. **Still open:** commission is not reserved (SD-99 (2)), so the gate is a one-time filter. A refund owed but not yet made is not read. SD-109 (2) is unchanged. An order with no pending or held row that names a vendor is corrected without a ledger read. With `FF_CARD_ORDER_LEDGER_V1` off the script still corrects no row that names a vendor. **For the operator, before `apply`:** (1) a review of this change that finds no order corrected; each of the last five reviews found one. (2) A dry run on a production copy, read line by line. Every `would correct` line is a vendor who will be debited the full commission later. Any line naming a CREATOR_COMMISSION leg, or an entry under a commission key, means a commission credit has landed somewhere, which SD-99 says cannot happen today: stop and find out why before going on. (3) Then `apply` once, immediately before the SD-99 repair deploys, away from :00. **Review (approve):** with the old entry-type exclusion put back and the key read emptied, a dry run corrects B, B2, C, D, D2 and D3 on Postgres; on the final tree all six are listed, each for its one reason. The reviewer read `creditCreatorCommission`, `createTransfer`, approve-held and `POST /admin/hawala/transfers` (every field of the commission leg is caller-supplied, and the admin route forwards all of them except the order id), and confirmed `createTransfer` is the only writer of ledger entries (one `createLedgerEntries` call site, no raw insert): it writes PENDING, moves balances in one transaction and marks COMPLETED separately, so counting PENDING, REVERSED and FAILED is the fail-closed choice. Its own probe on Postgres, dry run, orders through the real checkout: an entry under the row's key posted through the admin route off another seller's earnings and cut off PENDING; a two-level chain with an entry under the second row's key; and $1 off the vendor's earnings labelled REFUND are each listed; $1 into the vendor's earnings labelled CREATOR_COMMISSION, and an order with nothing, are corrected, as they should be. It agrees with listing another order's creator commission rather than correcting it (approve-held does not check that the other order's proceeds were in the vendor's earnings); the cost is that, once any commission credit has landed in production, every earlier attributed order of that vendor with a held row is listed. **For SD-99:** approve-held approves a row on whatever entry it is handed back, FAILED or hand-posted included; a Postgres case here pins that and will go red by design when approve-held is repaired. **Merged** (commits in the status cell). | fixed and merged (`72b0b43a`, `17e29cce`, `318b5372`, `9125d79a`, `db4882cb` on `claude/intelligent-mayer-7zymwu`, from `fix/p0-sd95-commission-legs` cc11f9a5); independent review: approve; Postgres 17/17, unit 53, mutation-checked. Another order's creator commission is now listed, not corrected, on purpose. **Script: dry run only** until the operator has read a dry run on a production copy. SD-99 (2) and SD-109 open; approve-held approving on a FAILED or hand-posted entry is pinned here for the SD-99 repair | `backend/src/scripts/{fix-creator-commission-minor-units.ts,README.md}`, `backend/src/modules/creator-attribution/minor-unit-correction.ts`, tests: `backend/src/scripts/__tests__/fix-creator-commission-minor-units.unit.spec.ts`, `backend/src/modules/creator-attribution/__tests__/minor-unit-correction.unit.spec.ts`, `backend/integration-tests/http/creator-commission-minor-units.spec.ts` |
| SD-126 | **Storefront sign-up never signed the buyer in, and pressing it again said the email was taken: it kept the registration token, which names no customer, as the session. Reported by a buyer on 2026-11-16 ("it told me I already have an account, but wouldn't send a link for forgot my password ... now I've got 2 emails on there but no access").** *Read, then pinned on Postgres (`store-signup-session.spec.ts`):* `POST /auth/customer/emailpass/register` answers a token with `actor_id` ""; `POST /store/customers` accepts it (`allowUnregistered`) and links the customer; `GET /store/customers/me` and `POST /store/carts/:id/customer` refuse it (401); `POST /auth/token/refresh` mints one that names the customer. `signup()` in `storefront/src/lib/data/customer.ts` kept the registration token, so the register page re-rendered the form with no message (`retrieveCustomerContext` got 401), `transferCart()` in the same `try` made the sign-up return "Unauthorized" when a cart existed, and a second press showed the backend's raw "Identity with email already exists". The account existed and its password would have worked on the login form, which is the likeliest explanation of the report (not confirmed against production). A sign-up whose second call failed (the shared auth limiter, a transient error) left a login with no profile; `login()` then told the buyer to register, and registering again did not answer "already exists": Medusa's emailpass provider re-passwords a login whose `app_metadata` is empty ("claimable", found later with SD-127), so the buyer came back to the same session problem. *The reset link:* Medusa emits `auth.password_reset` for any existing login, profile or not, for the lower-cased address, and `src/subscribers/password-reset.ts` hands it to the notification module (pinned, mailer stubbed). Candidates for the missing mail, none checked against production: `.env.production.example` named the sender `RESEND_FROM` while every reader uses `RESEND_FROM_EMAIL` (PRE_LAUNCH_AUDIT INFRA-5), so a deployment set up from it sends from `onboarding@resend.dev`, and Resend's documentation requires a domain you own and have verified; the subscriber drops the mail when `STOREFRONT_URL` is unset; and `POST /auth/*/reset-password` draws on the auth limiter's 20 a minute and the strict limiter's 5 per five minutes, keyed on the storefront server's address and so shared by every shopper (SD-33, SD-58). *Changed:* `signup()` creates the profile with the token register returned, refreshes it and keeps the refreshed token, which must name a customer; a failed cart transfer no longer fails sign-up; a taken email with the right password signs the buyer in, or finishes a login with no role at all, and refuses a vendor, staff or partner, or closed login with a message; a wrong password says the account exists and points at sign-in and "Forgot password?". `login()` decides from the token before storing any session, finishes a login with no role, and refuses the rest with a message; `RegisterForm` goes to `/user`. The sender is read as `RESEND_FROM_EMAIL`, else `RESEND_FROM` (`backend/src/lib/resend-sender.ts`), by the notification provider, the apprise service (bare address) and the admin seller-email route; the Resend provider warns at start-up on a resend.dev sender; the template names `RESEND_FROM_EMAIL`. *Reviews (an independent agent, three passes).* First: the sign-up form attached a shopper profile to vendor and staff logins, and the storefront's "Delete my account" deleted the shared login outright (reproduced on Postgres: the vendor's sign-in answered 401 afterwards); a login whose shopper profile was closed read as "try again" forever. Fixed: those logins get no profile, and `POST /store/customers/me/deletion` keeps a login that another actor uses (`backend/src/lib/login-shared.ts`), unlinking the profile (`customer_id: null`, as Medusa's `removeCustomerAccountWorkflow` does) and leaving the login's password history. Second: the first guard also kept a login with a PENDING vendor application, and anyone can file one against any login by email (SD-127), so a stranger could keep a shopper's login from ever being deleted (reproduced on Postgres); and a failed check became a permanent partial deletion. Fixed: only another actor link, or a vendor member row with the login's email, keeps a login; revoking a login deletes the vendor applications made with it that never became a vendor; a failed check answers 503 before anything is written. Third: approve; the older application type name `seller_creation` was missed (now matched), an approved application alone outlived the vendor (dropped, since the member row made by the same approval covers those vendors), rejected and cancelled applications were left behind (now deleted), and the storefront hid the 503's advice (now shown). *Proven:* `store-signup-session.spec.ts` on Postgres (9): the token contract, the taken-email refusal and sign-in, finishing an unfinished sign-up, the reset reaching the mailer with the storefront link, a vendor's login kept and still signing in, an application filed in a shopper's name not keeping the login and deleted with it (both type names), a vendor team member's login kept (email in another case), a failed check changing nothing and the retry going through, a shopper-only login revoked. Removing the guard, counting pending applications, or keeping on a failed check each fails its case. Storefront unit cases for every path (50); `login-shared` unit cases (13). | SD-149 | **Checkout, backend side: on a database built from the migrations no main checkout can complete, and Medusa's Stripe webhook refunds orders Mercur placed.** Found by the MVP sweep of 2026-11-17, which walked the storefront's own calls, call for call, on Postgres with only Stripe stubbed (the scout's spec and logs are kept in the session scratchpad). Every checkout spec installs a test-only BEFORE INSERT trigger to get past it (`cart-completion-refuses.spec.ts:40-52` and others), so no spec could see it; production runs `medusa db:migrate` (`scripts/railway-start.js`) and has no such trigger unless its schema differs. SD-53 mentioned the trigger only as found on the way. a definite "not available" left Delivery selected; the rule read a cart as complete when no line named a seller though an option was still listed; a second promotion code replaced the first; add to cart could show "Fetch failed."; the already-confirmed-card path re-enabled Place order at once. *Changed (15 commits, `8aa9fc42` … `f27ff565` on `claude/intelligent-mayer-7zymwu`, from `fix/p1-checkout-storefront`):* `lib/helpers/seller-shipping.ts` (a seller Mercur still lists is to choose for and named; a non-empty list is never complete; a method is paired with its seller when the buyer picked it on the page, any other counts for one seller; return options excluded), both buttons gated on it, lists memoized, type derived from the buyer's pick, no-options and unpriced-options notices; `tryAddToCart` returns the message as data, and only for an HTTP 4xx (`medusaError` keeps the status); `offeredAtCheckout` hides the manual provider outside `next dev`; `lib/data/delivery.ts` server actions; `lib/helpers/nothing-to-pay.ts`; `addPromotionCode`; a loading `Button` is disabled and the already-confirmed branch returns its completion. *Measured:* the store cart route with `+shipping_methods.shipping_option.seller.id` answers 500 "Cannot resolve alias path" (scratch spec, Postgres 16, not kept), so the field was not added to `CART_FIELDS`; `POST /store/carts/:id/complete-tickets` on a $0 all-ticket cart with no payment collection or session answers 200 with the order (total 0, no payment), the seat sold, Stripe never called, the same order on a second request, with `FF_TICKET_ORDER_SETTLEMENT_V1` on and off (scratch spec, not kept); `next build` with the Docker build stage's env compiles `offeredAtCheckout(…,"production")` at both call sites. *Decided:* the delivery-zone check is a nudge, not a block, because nothing downstream enforces the zones and a postal code is placed at its ZIP3 centroid unless the spatial geocoder is on: `DELIVERY_NOT_AVAILABLE` pre-selects Pickup, else Shipping, once per answer, with the reason kept in view and Delivery still choosable; `DELIVERY_ZONES_UNAVAILABLE` shows nothing; a failed check is reported and moves nobody. A $0 cart that is not all tickets is told it cannot be placed yet (the main checkout answers 409 `cart_nothing_to_pay`, backend bf22e8ed); free checkout on the main route is a follow-up. A promotion code is added to the codes the cart has, which makes typed codes stack: Medusa applies every code that produces an adjustment and has no exclusivity rule, the API always accepted several, and the old field allowed one typed code at a time only because each replaced the last. The owner has not confirmed stacking. The field has no control to take a code off (`deletePromotionCode` has no caller). *Free-shipping codes (read in Medusa 2.14.2 and Mercur 1.5.0, not changed):* `POST /store/carts/:id { promo_codes }` runs `updateCartPromotionsWorkflow` with REPLACE and keeps only codes that produced an adjustment on the cart as it is; the promotion field is on the cart page, before any shipping method exists, so a shipping-only code is dropped, and later refreshes re-apply only kept codes. Applying it at checkout is not a storefront fix: `splitAndCompleteCartWorkflow` creates each seller order's shipping method without its adjustments and authorizes each order's split payment at that order's total, so the discount would come off the card charge and not off the orders. | SD-157 | **The seventeen vendor-panel files that import `lib/sdk` (invoicing, POS, farm, cottage food, digital products, bug report) now send the seller's JWT from the panel's one token store, as `fetchQuery` does; a 401 drops the stored token only if it is unchanged since the request read it; no write is retried and Record Payment cannot be double-sent; and two visible panel bugs found on the way are fixed (SD-146).** *Before:* `lib/sdk.ts` was a second JS SDK with `auth: { type: "session" }`. The SDK (2.14.2, read) sends no Authorization header for a session client, the panel never makes a session, and Mercur's `checkSellerApproved` (b2c-core 1.5.0, read) reads only the Authorization header, so the 39 calls in those files were refused (by reading), and the SDK, which does nothing on a 401, left the token. *The rest of the panel (read):* the token lives in `localStorage` under "medusa_auth_token" (`setAuthToken` at sign-in, `clearAuthToken`); `fetchQuery` sends it unless `isPublicAuthRoute` exempts the path and drops it on any other 401; the panel's own JWT SDK (`lib/client`, 54 files) reads the same key per request and does nothing on a 401; `ProtectedRoute` sends a seller with no token to `/login`, the route ErrorBoundary sends a thrown `FetchError` 401 there, and the query client never retries a query on a 401; nothing refreshes tokens. *Fixed:* `lib/sdk` exports `client.fetch` over the panel's own JWT SDK instance (one instance, one store), sets Authorization from one read of the store (null, which the SDK deletes, on an exempt route; a caller's header wins, as in `fetchQuery`), and on a `FetchError` 401 from a route that is not exempt drops the stored token only if it is unchanged since the request read it, then rethrows the error unchanged. The comparison is with the stored token, not with the Authorization the request carried: a caller's own header (`invites.tsx` sends one to `/vendor/invites/accept` through `fetchQuery`) still lets a 401 drop an unchanged stored token. `fetchQuery` gets the same check: a 401 that arrived after a new sign-in emptied the store (the review measured it in `lib/sdk` and read it in `fetchQuery`; the spec now measures both). Mutations no longer retry: the query client's default retried each failed write once, and the review measured a 204 DELETE and a POS order on a 502 each sent twice, which would duplicate POS orders, invoices, cottage-food sales, farm records and POS checkout's earnings transfer, which takes no idempotency key; queries keep their rule. Record Payment had no pending guard, unlike Issue Invoice, so a double-click sent two requests, and since the backend accepts a payment on a paid invoice only the key `${id}:${amount}` kept a second payment row out; every Record Payment button is now disabled while a payment is in flight. The lot form's allocations are now exactly the backend's `lot_allocation_enum` (`RETAIL`, `RESTAURANT`, `WHOLESALE`, `CSA`, `COOPERATIVE`, `DONATION`, `PROCESSING`): the panel had `kitchen` (no equivalent) and `restaurant` in lower case, which the insert refuses (by reading, 500 "Failed to create lot"), and a default, `LotAllocation.RETAIL`, it did not define (TS2339); the lot page now labels every value and shows the raw value otherwise (the re-review found the change safe for stored data). `/bug-report`, the user menu's link, had no route and landed on the no-match page; it is now routed inside the signed-in layout. The page's POST has `bugReportSchema`'s shape, but four boundary checks differ, each answered 400 "Validation failed" and shown as the toast "Bug report failed" with that message, which names no field: the form checks the lengths of `summary` (5) and `description` (10) before trimming, while the backend trims first; it does not cap `category` at 60; and it does not cap the screenshot's filename at 120. Chosen over moving the calls onto `fetchQuery`, which is typed for GET, POST and DELETE only (invoicing PATCHes, farm PUTs) and throws plain Errors with no `status`. As with `fetchQuery`, after a 401 the seller reaches `/login` on the layout's next render. **Proven (vitest with a mocked fetch, no browser), 61 tests in six specs:** `src/lib/sdk.spec.tsx` 31: the bearer is the stored token, read per request and equal to `fetchQuery`'s; exempt routes get none from either client and a caller's header wins in both; with no token none goes out and the layout redirects; a refused token is dropped, then the layout redirects; across 401, 403, 404 and 500 and the exempt routes both clients send the same header and leave the same token; a network error, an abort and an unparseable 204 leave it in both; a 401 after a newer sign-in keeps the newer token in both; and a TypeScript walk of the source finds no `type: "session"`, SDK clients made only in `lib/client` (dynamic imports count), both JWT, no SDK re-export in any file, `lib/client` included, its SDK import used only after `new`, no `new` on anything imported from `lib/client`, exactly the seventeen `lib/sdk` importers, no raw fetch in them and none without an Authorization header elsewhere except `fetchQuery`'s and the dead digital-products form's, and `publicAuthSdk` only in sign-in. `src/lib/query-client.spec.tsx` 9: through the app's query client, a POS order on 502, POS checkout on 500, an invoice on a network error, a cottage-food profile on 504, a `fetchQuery` write on 502 and a farm DELETE on 204 are each sent once, and a walk finds no `retry` reaching a mutation. `src/hooks/api/invoicing.spec.tsx` 3: the finances page's real hooks send the bearer to the routes the backend serves with the bodies they read. `src/routes/finances/record-payment.spec.tsx` 3: the real invoicing section enables Record Payment with no payment in flight, disables every one while one is, and a double-click calls the mutation once. `src/routes/farm/lot-allocation.spec.tsx` 12: the values equal the backend model's and migration's in this checkout, every value has a label, the lot page shows each, and the form sends `RETAIL`. `src/routes/bug-report/bug-report.spec.tsx` 3: against the real `RouteMap`, `/bug-report` loads the page inside ProtectedRoute and MainLayout, every literal link in the user menu reaches a page, and the page POSTs `/vendor/bug-report` with the bearer. The original session client fails 21 of the 61; the shipped bundle had `auth:{type:"session"}` and has none. Mutations, each failing its cases, three rounds: the session client (21), the one-line `type: "jwt"` (5), header stripped (8), no 401 handling (4), a wrapper over `publicAuthSdk` (8), a second JWT client (9), drop on any error (3), drop on exempt routes (2), `publicAuthSdk` set to session (2), another client-making file (1), `"session" as const` (1), layout not redirecting (2); the old mutation retry rule (8), a hook, an inline page mutation, `setMutationDefaults` or a caller putting a retry back (2, 1, 1, 1); the previous wrapper (4), `fetchQuery` or `lib/sdk` without the late-401 check (1 each), clearing on any non-`FetchError` (3), the token to exempt routes (3), overriding a caller's header (1);
