| SD-158 | **Two vendor routes let one store write another store's records: `POST /vendor/nursery/products`, live behind `FF_NURSERY_VERTICAL_V1` and `vendor.nursery`, and `POST /vendor/order-cycles/:id/products`, inert on today's schema for SD-63's missing column. The sweep found the same fault in the exchange-products POST (inert for the same column) and a cross-store read in the fees POST (live on today's schema). All four now act only on the caller's store's records.** *Found* (SD-156 final review, Postgres): the nursery POST found the row by the body's `product_id` alone and spread the body, `seller_id` included, into the write (B got 201 on A's row, read A's `cost_to_produce` 1.25, re-owned it, overwrote `hardiness_zone`, and created a row on another of A's products); the cycle POST took any variant id and updated the cycle's row for it (participant B set coordinator A's row to price 0.01, quantity 0 and hidden, and listed another of A's variants under itself). *Sweep:* the exchange-products POST did the same through the service's upsert on (cycle, variant) and stamped `exchange.seller_id \|\| caller`, so a coordinator could also create rows in a participant's name; the fees POST attached any store's template and answered with its name and amount, inserting before the lookup (an id naming nothing left a row and a 500 with the lookup's text). *Changed:* a store's keys are its id and its members' ids, removed members included (`shared/store-keys.ts`, the rekey script's mapping), because the routes wrote member ids until SD-145 and the rekey moves them only when `apply` runs (and leaves rows whose member matches nothing); a row under one of the store's keys is the store's, is listed, and is updated in place with the store's id set. Nursery: the product must be the store's (`seller_product`), `seller_id` is the gate's, the body is an allow-list (one string per id, an array is 400); a row is the store's only when its key and its product are the store's: PUT/DELETE answer `forbidden()` for any other, missing included (was 404), PUT writes attribute columns only, GET lists only those rows. A row another store wrote on the owner's product is soft-deleted, its values kept for forensics, and a fresh row is made for the owner with only what the owner sent (the unique index is partial). Order cycles: every variant must be the store's and the row written is matched by cycle, variant and the store's keys, the coordinator included; the store's variant held by another store's row is 409, not replaced (the row carries the cycle's sales); exchange products go only on the caller's own exchange (its keys), all checked before any write; DELETE answers `forbidden()` for a missing row, another cycle's row, and (for a participant) another store's row (was 404/404/403); fees take only the coordinator's own templates (its keys), checked before the insert, and GET reads back only those. A create that loses a race is tried once more and updates the row the other write made (was a fixed 500; measured bursts of 8 now give 8×201 and one row). *Coordinator:* own rows only for create and update; removal of any row kept (DELETE docstring, `docs/CDFI_COOP_ROADMAP.md`). Nothing grants setting another store's price, quantity or visibility: `addProductToOrderCycle` stamped the caller only on create and updated whatever row matched, the old exchange route's coordinator path created rows in a participant's name (now refused), the panel's products section offers only the store's products, and `docs/CSA_NETWORK_POSITIONING.md` lists only add and remove. The panel's exchanges section now offers "Add Products" only on the viewer's own exchange (`order-cycle-exchanges-section.tsx`). Touched routes answer fixed messages and log the error (`shared/route-input.ts`). **Measured on today's schema** (SD-158 review, no SD-63 columns): cycle writes fail closed with fixed messages, while reads, DELETE and the 409 work. **Proven** in `integration-tests/http/vendor-cross-store-writes.spec.ts` (24 cases, real Postgres, two stores with member tokens, rows asserted after every refusal, including member-keyed and removed-member rows, the soft-deleted takeover, bursts of 8, and the three operator queries; SD-63's `raw_override_price` and `raw_amount` added as a fixture, to remove when SD-63 merges); `vendor-store-keying` (8) and `vendor-quest-flows` (1, now on a real store product) pass; unit 1050/1050, posture-a 61/61; panel 221/221. *Mutation-checked:* first round 26 integration and 11 unit; review round 25 integration over 4 runs, 6 unit and 2 panel; each failed its own case. **Operator:** run the nursery query and keep its rows before deploy: it filters `deleted_at IS NULL`, so once an owner's POST replaces a planted row the query stops listing it; afterwards the replaced rows are exactly this table's soft-deleted rows (`SELECT * FROM nursery_product_attribute WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL`, matched to the warn log's `replaced_row_id`; the DELETE route hard-deletes, measured). Nursery: `SELECT npa.id, npa.product_id, npa.seller_id, sp.seller_id AS product_owner FROM nursery_product_attribute npa LEFT JOIN "member" m ON m.id = npa.seller_id LEFT JOIN seller_seller_product_product sp ON sp.product_id = npa.product_id AND sp.deleted_at IS NULL WHERE npa.deleted_at IS NULL AND sp.seller_id IS DISTINCT FROM (CASE WHEN left(npa.seller_id, 4) = 'mem_' THEN m.seller_id ELSE npa.seller_id END);` Cycle products: `SELECT ocp.id, ocp.order_cycle_id, ocp.variant_id, ocp.seller_id, sp.seller_id AS variant_owner FROM order_cycle_product ocp LEFT JOIN "member" m ON m.id = ocp.seller_id LEFT JOIN product_variant pv ON pv.id = ocp.variant_id LEFT JOIN seller_seller_product_product sp ON sp.product_id = pv.product_id AND sp.deleted_at IS NULL WHERE ocp.deleted_at IS NULL AND sp.seller_id IS DISTINCT FROM (CASE WHEN left(ocp.seller_id, 4) = 'mem_' THEN m.seller_id ELSE ocp.seller_id END);` Cycle fees: `SELECT ocf.id, ocf.order_cycle_id, ef.seller_id AS template_owner, oc.coordinator_seller_id FROM order_cycle_fee ocf JOIN order_cycle oc ON oc.id = ocf.order_cycle_id LEFT JOIN enterprise_fee ef ON ef.id = ocf.enterprise_fee_id LEFT JOIN "member" m ON m.id = ef.seller_id LEFT JOIN "member" cm ON cm.id = oc.coordinator_seller_id WHERE ocf.deleted_at IS NULL AND (CASE WHEN left(ef.seller_id, 4) = 'mem_' THEN m.seller_id ELSE ef.seller_id END) IS DISTINCT FROM (CASE WHEN left(oc.coordinator_seller_id, 4) = 'mem_' THEN cm.seller_id ELSE oc.coordinator_seller_id END);` (each proven by a spec case). **Re-review (approve at `0287a481`, measured on Postgres):** a removed member's and a dangling `mem_` id's cycle rows are neither listed nor deletable by another participant, while a participant's own member-keyed row is; a create that fails for another reason is tried twice then answers the fixed 500; on today's schema both cycle writes still fail closed. **Limits the re-review measured or read:** a row another store planted before the fix under the owner's own key (its store id, which is public, or one of its member ids) cannot be told from the owner's row, is listed to the owner and keeps the injected values, and no operator query finds it; | SD-159 | **The vendor panel half of SD-151: a newly approved vendor could not get from sign-in to a product a buyer could purchase, and the panel said it had.** Fixed on `fix/p0-onboarding-panel` (25 commits on `65fba793`, SD-157), by specs with a mocked `fetch`; an independent review then ran the panel's exact calls on Postgres (at 0a40983c) and pickup only, flat rate only, and both with lost answers each ended in a real buyer order. The third round's changes (regions and currency, handles, refresh failures, Settings names) were measured on Postgres by the re-review at a71a6a2c, with the panel's own `selling-setup.ts`, `seller-token.ts` and product-create code driving the backend: a US store and a Canadian store (added region in CAD) each completed real buyer orders, and the earlier false-ready cases now read not ready with the reason. (1) *Token:* when the session or the registration status says approved and the stored JWT names no actor, the panel sends `POST /auth/token/refresh` and stores the answer only if it names one; a 401, or a 2xx whose token names no actor, signs the vendor out to `/login` with a message and that token is never sent again (`lib/seller-token.ts`); a 429, a 5xx or a network error is not a refusal: the refresh shares the 20-a-minute `POST /auth/*` limiter with sign-in (measured: both answered 429 together), so the protected layout and the pending-approval page show the reason with a retry and the next read asks again; the pending-approval page also drops a session cached while pending, which sent "Check Status" after approval back and forth. (2) *Features:* a seller's default features are the vendor type's and the playbook recipe's together (the assignment is read from `GET /vendor/playbook/assign`), so nothing shown before goes away and single-role Hub, Commons and Grove gain Products, Cottage Food, Promotions, Price Lists and Reviews (and the plan-gated Nursery and Production Ledger), Kitchen gains Shows, Service gains Order Cycles, Creator gains Order Cycles and Shows; a seller's own selection still wins; a spec reads only the feature keys of `backend/src/modules/playbook/recipes/*.ts` (it tolerates the `default_listing_type` that `fix/p0-onboarding-backend` adds) and holds the panel's mirror exact for all eleven. *Open product question:* whether the menus should later be trimmed to the recipe, which would take Volunteers, Donations, Aid Network and Funds & Grants from Hub and Kitchen, Order Cycles from Kitchen, Delivery Orders and Delivery Zones from Grove and Commons, and Products and Inventory from Service (whose recipe has no Products although the backend takes its listings). (3) *Buyable:* `lib/selling-setup.ts` reads a stock location linked to the sales channel; a shipping option on it whose service zone covers a country of a region (`GET /vendor/regions`) and which has a price that region's carts are charged, in its currency and with no rule narrowing it to another region or a cart total (options read with `*prices.price_rules`); and a published product with a price in the currency of a region offered delivery, untracked or in stock at a linked location (the first 3 published products, 5 variants each). The product form asks for stock and names where it is held, or lets the vendor not track it, and writes the levels against each variant's `variant_rank`. The dashboard leaves setup only when that readiness holds or the store has an order; readiness does not look at shipping profiles (the review measured orders completing with the product on no profile, the store's default, or a profile no option has) or past the first products. (4) *Wizard:* the listing step creates a draft through the product form's hook and payload (price in major units, in the currency of the stock location's region, else the first region's), with an uploaded photo in place of a pasted URL; the delivery step is the guided setup; publish publishes that product, refuses to record it unless the status answer shows it published, and records it with no typed id; "You're live!" is said only when readiness holds; the copy promises no shipping option, download link, contact link or ticket. *Handles:* product handles are unique across the marketplace (measured: a second store's "Pat's Pickles" got 400 "Product with handle: pats-pickles, already exists."), so the product form and the wizard send `<title>-<store handle>` (from `GET /vendor/sellers/me`), with `-2`, `-3`… on a clash inside the store, and a typed handle as typed; when a create fails the store's products are read again and the product a lost answer made, under the handle just sent, is used instead of the error (measured without: the resend got the same 400 and left the draft behind); within one press nothing is sent twice (measured). ## Security hardening (production-readiness pass 2026-06-20)

Closes the gaps from the security review. All landed on branch
`claude/fbm-production-readiness-h4lywz`.

| # | Item | Resolution | Location |
|---|------|------------|----------|
| ~~SH-1~~ | Centralized error-response sanitizer (prevent field/query/stack leakage in API errors) | **done** — new `sanitizedErrorHandler()` wraps Medusa's canonical `errorHandler` (reuses its error-type→status mapping, no drift) and, **in production only**, rewrites `status >= 500` response bodies to a generic message while logging the full error via the structured logger and forwarding to Sentry. 4xx client errors (validation / not-found / auth) pass through unchanged; dev/test stays verbose. Wired as `errorHandler` in `defineMiddlewares`. Unit-tested (prod 5xx redaction, 4xx passthrough, dev verbosity). | `backend/src/shared/error-sanitizer.ts`, `backend/src/api/middlewares.ts`, `backend/src/shared/__tests__/error-sanitizer.unit.spec.ts` |
| ~~SH-2~~ | Explicit session-cookie timeout + flags | **done** — added `projectConfig.cookieOptions` (`httpOnly`, `secure` in prod, `sameSite: "lax"`, `maxAge` 24h) and `projectConfig.sessionOptions.ttl` (24h) so the admin/vendor `connect.sid` session cookie is hardened and no longer lives indefinitely. `sameSite: lax` is safe for the subdomain layout (admin/api share the `freeblackmarket.com` site); CSRF guard still enforces same-origin on writes. | `backend/medusa-config.ts` |

## D8 — Duplication across the ask/in-kind surfaces (2026-09-09)

**What D8 means.** `REPO_CONSOLIDATION_REVIEW.md`'s decision table defines D8 as
the hygiene/consolidation decision: duplication executed on where safe, queued
where riskier. This section is the queued half for one family of duplication
that the CDFI/co-op roadmap (§3.8) asked to have recorded rather than resolved.
Nothing here is a bug; each entry is a place where two or more systems model the
same real thing with different vocabularies, and where a future consolidation
has to pick one.

Found while building the FBM→Blackout mutual-aid seam, and **verified against
the code rather than transcribed** — the roadmap said "three in-kind intake
vocabularies" and there are four.

| # | Item | Status | Location |
|---|------|--------|----------|
| D8-1 | **Four "ask" stores across two repos, no shared vocabulary.** FBM `mutual_aid_request` (a person asks for help; OPEN/MATCHED/FULFILLED/WITHDRAWN/EXPIRED) · FBM `demand_post` (a group asks for supply; OPEN/THRESHOLD_MET/NEGOTIATING/EXPIRED) · Blackout `coalition_aid_posts` (need\|offer; open/in_progress/fulfilled/expired/cancelled) · Blackout `coalition_needs` (a coalition asks for a thing; open/claimed/fulfilled/closed). Four status vocabularies for four shapes of the same verb, and the FBM→Blackout mirror already has to map one onto another at the seam. **Near-miss to keep out of it:** FBM's `request` module is an RFQ/quote table whose docstring name-drops mutual aid; it is a buyer→vendor price request and shares no vocabulary with any of the above. | **deferred (L)** | `backend/src/modules/{mutual-aid,demand-pool}/models/`, blackout `packages/api/src/db/migrations/{020,054}_*.up.sql` |
| D8-2 | **Four in-kind intake vocabularies, only one of which records provenance.** FBM `intake_receipt` has a real taxonomy — `source` (donation/rescue/gleaning/overproduction/transfer_in), `donor_type` (individual/business/farm/organization/anonymous), plus `estimated_value_cents` with a `valuation_basis`. FBM `mutual_aid_offer.category` is free text with no source or valuation concept at all. Blackout `coalition_aid_posts.category` is a closed set of ten (food/transport/labor/materials/care/housing/childcare/eldercare/tech_support/other). Blackout `coalition_needs.kind` is free TEXT with a seven-value `SUGGESTED_NEED_KINDS` UI hint. The mirror maps FBM's free text onto Blackout's closed ten with an `other` fallback, which is the safe direction but is lossy and one-way. | **deferred (M)** | `backend/src/modules/aid-network/models/intake-receipt.ts`, `backend/src/modules/mutual-aid/models/mutual-aid-offer.ts`, blackout `packages/core/src/coalition/{mutualAid,needs}.ts` |
| D8-3 | **Two ways to record value that did not move as cash, neither aware of the other.** `RAIL_REGISTRY.GIFT` is `closed_loop: true` with `account_type: null` — it deliberately carries no balances — so the barter-accept route writes a zero-amount `TRANSFER` tagged `metadata.intended_rail: "GIFT"` and says so in a comment, because `createTransfer` takes no `currency_code` and GIFT-denominated accounts do not exist. Meanwhile `intake_receipt.estimated_value_cents` records an in-kind valuation for donor acknowledgment and contribution reporting, deliberately outside the money ledgers. Both are "value that is real but not cash"; they share no type, no unit, and no reporting path. Resolving means deciding whether GIFT gets an account type or whether in-kind valuation stays wholly outside the ledger — an accounting decision, not a refactor. | **deferred (L)** | `backend/src/modules/hawala-ledger/rails.ts`, `backend/src/api/store/collective/demand-pools/[id]/barter/[proposalId]/accept/route.ts`, `backend/src/modules/aid-network/models/intake-receipt.ts` |

## D9 — Order-cycle sale accounting (2026-09-09)

Filed while giving `subscribers/order-cycle-order-placed.ts` its first producer.
That subscriber has always been complete — it records each sale against the
cycle product and links the order to the cycle — and nothing ever wrote the key
it reads, so it returned at its first guard on every order ever placed. Making
it fire for the first time makes the rows below **reachable**; none of them is
introduced by that change, and none is fixable without a decision.

| # | Item | Status | Location |
|---|------|--------|----------|
| ~~D9-1~~ | ~~**A cycle can oversell.**~~ — **closed 2026-09-13, in two layers, because it was two bugs.** **The one nobody had named: a lost update.** `recordSale` read `sold_quantity`, added, and wrote the sum back, so two buyers completing at once both read the same starting value and the second write erased the first. The cycle oversold *and* under-recorded that it had, which is why the counter could not be trusted to detect the problem it was causing. `applySoldQuantity` now issues one `UPDATE ... SET sold_quantity = sold_quantity + ? ... RETURNING`, which cannot lose a concurrent increment. `sold_quantity` is a plain integer with no `raw_` sibling, the condition `demand-pool` checks before doing the same thing. **The one the row described: prevention.** The audit said a real fix is an inventory decision — reserve at add-to-cart, or fail at completion — and the decision taken is **fail at completion**. Reserving when an item enters a cart needs expiry and release machinery, and an abandoned cart then holds a grower's produce until it times out; for short perishable cycles that is worse than the problem, since the stock is unavailable to everyone while nobody is buying it. Failing at completion costs a buyer a late refusal and never costs a producer a sale they could have made. `workflows/hooks/validate-order-cycle.ts` runs on `completeCartWorkflow.hooks.validate` — before payment, which is the point. **What deliberately survives:** two buyers completing in the same instant both read the same remaining quantity and both pass. That residue cannot be removed without reservations, so it is handled where it lands rather than pretended away — the increment is atomic so neither sale is lost, and crossing capacity is logged as a warning naming the cycle, variant and amount over, for a coordinator to refund or source more. **And the post-payment path records an overshoot rather than refusing one**, on purpose: it runs from `order.placed`, after the buyer has paid, so refusing would leave the money taken, the order real, and the cycle unaware of an order someone has to pack — and would desynchronise `sold_quantity` from the `order_cycle_sale` rows written moments earlier for D9-2. 20 tests across `__tests__/record-sale-atomic` and `workflows/hooks/__tests__/validate-order-cycle`. — **2026-11-15: the preventable half is not enforced on any storefront cycle sale, because the order-cycle guard does not run on Mercur's main checkout (SD-72 (a)).** — **2026-11-17 (merged): enforced on storefront cycle sales; the order-cycle guard runs in front of Mercur's main checkout (SD-147), and an oversold line is refused 400 with no order, measured on Postgres. The two-buyers race, the no-cart-lock race and buyer-writable line tags remain.** | done |
| ~~D9-2~~ | ~~**`recordSale` is not idempotent and the subscriber does not dedupe.** A retried or duplicated `order.placed` double-increments `sold_quantity`. The sibling `subscribers/cottage-food-record-sale.ts` solves exactly this by making its own `recordSale` idempotent on `(source, source_id)`; order-cycle has no such key, so matching that pattern means a schema change.~~ — **fixed 2026-09-10.** The schema change this row anticipated: a new `order_cycle_sale` ledger keyed on `(order_cycle_id, variant_id, source, source_id)`, following cottage-food's shape so the two modules dedupe the same way. Per variant rather than per order, because one order can contain several variants from the same cycle and each is its own sale. **The guarantee is a partial unique index, not the service's read-then-write check** — two concurrent deliveries of the same event both pass that check, so uniqueness has to live in the database; a `23505` is caught and read as "already recorded". Partial on `source_id IS NOT NULL`, because a manual adjustment carries no source id and two identical manual corrections are two corrections, so that path stays deliberately non-idempotent. The ledger records `quantity` as well as the key, so `sold_quantity` can be rebuilt from it if it ever drifts. Additive migration: no change to `order_cycle_product`, nothing to backfill. Sales placed before the migration have no ledger row, so a duplicate delivery of a *pre-existing* order could still double-count once — accepted rather than backfilled, since D9-4's link is itself only recently populated. | done | `backend/src/modules/order-cycle/models/order-cycle-sale.ts`, `backend/src/modules/order-cycle/service.ts`, `backend/src/subscribers/order-cycle-order-placed.ts` |
| ~~D9-3~~ | ~~**A closed cycle still accepts sales.**~~ — **closed 2026-09-13.** The half this row called "the real gap" — a cart tagged with a cycle that closed hours earlier, which is not a race but a missing check — is now checked in `workflows/hooks/validate-order-cycle.ts`, composed into `complete-cart-validate.ts` as the row said it would have to be. A cart naming a cycle that is not `open`, or that no longer exists, is refused before payment. **The policy question the row deferred is answered, and the two ends now differ on purpose.** Checkout refuses a closed cycle; the `order.placed` subscriber still records against one. That is not a contradiction: refusing *before* the buyer pays costs them a message, while refusing *after* they have paid would lose a real sale to a sweep that closed the cycle mid-checkout. The rule is that the last moment before money moves is where a cycle's state is enforced, and the subscriber's existing three tests pinning the permissive behaviour stay valid rather than being inverted. The validator also refuses an item the cycle no longer offers, and sums a variant across cart lines before comparing — two lines individually inside capacity and jointly over it would otherwise both pass. — **2026-11-15: not enforced on storefront cycle sales; the guard does not run on Mercur's main checkout (SD-72 (a)).** — **2026-11-17 (merged): enforced on storefront cycle sales; a closed or missing cycle is refused 400 at the main checkout before Mercur authorizes (SD-147).** | done |
| ~~D9-4~~ | ~~**The order↔cycle remote link is write-only.** The subscriber creates it and nothing in the repo reads it. It is the natural source for the `ordersPlaced` field that FBM's §3 `cycle.close` event deliberately omits (`docs/contracts/blackout-integration.md`), which is now unblocked because the link finally has real rows in it.~~ — **fixed 2026-09-10.** `countCycleOrders` in `backend/src/lib/blackout-cycle.ts` counts the link rows for a cycle and the sweep attaches the result to `cycle.close`. Three choices worth keeping: it reads the **link** rather than the new `order_cycle_sale` ledger, because a sale row exists only for variants registered in the cycle while the link is written for every order tagged with it; it is sent on **close only**, matching Blackout's renderer, since a cycle that just opened has had no chance to take orders; and a failed read yields **`undefined`, not `0`** — Blackout drops the clause on `undefined` and prints "0 order(s) placed" on `0`, so collapsing the two would announce a confident falsehood in a vendor's room. A genuine zero is still sent as zero. The link is only recently populated, so cycles that ran before the storefront started tagging line items will under-report; not backfillable, since the tag was never written. | done | `backend/src/lib/blackout-cycle.ts`, `backend/src/jobs/order-cycle-status-update.ts`, `docs/contracts/blackout-integration.md` |
| ~~D9-5~~ | ~~**Cart metadata does not survive FBM's checkout.** `@mercurjs/b2c-core` overrides `POST /store/carts/:id/complete` with `splitAndCompleteCartWorkflow`, which builds its order payload by hand and never copies `cart.metadata` onto the orders — it fetches the field (`completeCartFields` includes it) and drops it. Line-item metadata it does carry. This is why the order-cycle producer writes to the line item. **Anything else in this repo that stamps cart metadata and expects to read it off the order is silently broken on the main checkout path** — `storefront/src/lib/data/donations.ts` and the cart `tier` route are the ones to audit first. FBM's other completion routes wrap Medusa's own `completeCartWorkflow` and do propagate, so behaviour differs by checkout path.~~ — **fixed 2026-09-10, and the audit it asked for was done.** `backend/src/lib/cart-metadata-recovery.ts` recovers a cart's metadata from any order it produced (order → `order_set` → `cart_id` → cart), because the drop is in a vendored workflow and this repo recovers rather than patches. Order metadata still wins per key; the cart read is skipped only when the order already carries **every** key asked for, since skipping on any one of them would let a partially-stamped order discard the rest. **The audit found three consumers, not one, and all three were silently broken on the main checkout path:** donations never accrued (`donation-order-accrued.ts`); last-click affiliate attribution never happened, so a creator whose link drove a sale earned nothing while promo-code attribution kept working off `order.promotions` and masked it (`attribute-order-on-placed.ts`); and every POS, vending and pickup sale resolved to the `online` default, which is worse than a missing number because the channel report looked complete (`attribute-channel-on-placed.ts`). The cart `tier` route the row named is **not** affected: nothing reads `order.metadata.tier`, and the per-item `sliding_scale_tier` stamp survives on line items regardless. | done | `backend/src/lib/cart-metadata-recovery.ts`, `backend/src/subscribers/donation-order-accrued.ts`, `backend/src/subscribers/attribute-order-on-placed.ts`, `backend/src/subscribers/attribute-channel-on-placed.ts` |
| ~~D9-6~~ | ~~**`link-booking-on-order-placed` can never fire.**~~ — **loop closed 2026-09-13.** The id existed only in a query string: `GET /store/embed/bookings` returned a checkout URL with `?booking_id=`, and the string appeared in exactly one place in the repo, so no booking was ever linked to an order, none confirmed, and no customer ever got the confirmation email. Three pieces, built to mirror the affiliate path rather than invent a second one: the storefront middleware pins `?booking_id=` to a `_fbm_booking` cookie (24h, not the affiliate cookie's 90 days — a booking is a slot at a time, and a stale id in a long cookie would attach a months-old reservation to an unrelated purchase); `applyBookingToCart` POSTs it from the cart loader, beside `applyAttributionToCart` and idempotent for the same reason; and `POST /store/carts/:id/booking` **validates before writing** — `booking_id` is caller-supplied, and writing it through unread would let anyone stamp someone else's booking onto their own cart and have the subscriber confirm it on payment, so an unknown, cancelled, or already-ordered booking is refused. The subscriber now reads through `getOrderCartMetadata` rather than `order.metadata` directly, since `splitAndCompleteCartWorkflow` drops cart metadata at checkout (D9-5) and would have broken the loop again at the last step. 8 tests. | done |

**The audit this row asked for was done, and it was worse than "silently broken" implies.** `storefront/src/lib/data/donations.ts` `setCartDonationPreferences` writes `donation_total`, `donation_beneficiary_id` and `storefront_id` onto the cart. `subscribers/donation-order-accrued.ts` read them off `order.metadata` on `order.placed`, found nothing, and hit its own `if (!beneficiaryId || donationTotal <= 0) return`. So **a buyer who chose to donate at checkout had their donation silently never accrued** — no error, no log, the beneficiary's `accrued_balance` simply never moved. A money-adjacent promise failing quietly is worse than one failing loudly.

Verified rather than inferred: the vendored `split-and-complete-cart.js` order payload was read directly and has **no `metadata` key at all** (line items and shipping methods carry theirs; the cart's is dropped).

Fixed by recovery, not by patching the dependency. The same workflow calls `createOrderSetStep({ cart_id: cart.id, ... })` and `order_set` is linked to its orders, so the originating cart is reachable: order → order_set → `cart_id` → `cart.metadata`. `lib/cart-metadata-recovery.ts` `getOrderCartMetadata` does that walk, lets the order's own metadata win on any key it carries (a correctly-propagating checkout path, or an operator edit, should not be overridden), skips both queries entirely when the order already has the data, and never throws — it runs inside an `order.placed` subscriber, where failing to recover an optional preference must not fail the order. A test reverting the subscriber to the old read confirms the regression is caught.

**Still open:** the drop itself, and any *other* consumer. `backend/src/api/store/carts/[id]/tier/route.ts` stamps cart metadata and has not been traced to a reader. New consumers should use `getOrderCartMetadata` rather than reading `order.metadata` directly. | **partly fixed (L)** | `backend/src/lib/cart-metadata-recovery.ts`, `backend/src/subscribers/donation-order-accrued.ts`, `backend/node_modules/@mercurjs/b2c-core/.medusa/server/src/workflows/cart/workflows/split-and-complete-cart.js`, `backend/src/api/store/carts/[id]/tier/route.ts` |

## D10 — Unauthenticated reads on the community `/store` surfaces (2026-09-10)

`api/middlewares.ts` `COMMUNITY_WRITE_PREFIXES` authenticates about fourteen
`/store/*` prefixes for `COMMUNITY_WRITE_VERBS` — POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE —
and nothing else. Browsing those surfaces is meant to be public, so **GET was
never covered**. The prefix list gates *verbs, not data sensitivity*, and
several of those GETs return whole ORM entities by spreading them
(`...order`, `...delivery`, `...courier`, `...producer`) or project a
`customer_id` next to behavioural data. Two files make the gap visible in
place: `delivery-batches/[id]/route.ts` and `volunteer-logs/route.ts` each
enforce authorization in the write handler and none in the read handler
beside it.

Found while fixing D10-1. Ids are enumerable throughout: each prefix's own
unauthenticated list endpoint supplies them.

| ID | Finding | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ~~D10-1~~ | ~~`GET /store/food-producers/:id/orders` — unauthenticated, no actor check, returning `recipient_name`, `recipient_phone`, `recipient_email`, `delivery_address_line_1/2`, `customer_notes` for every order of any producer. The sibling `orders/:orderId` route already checked ownership; only the list route was missed.~~ — **fixed 2026-09-10**: owner-only via a new `actorOwnsResource`, which unlike `actorMayManage` does **not** grandfather a null `owner_id`. Grandfathering is defensible for a write (middleware authenticates write verbs) but not for a read of a third party's address, where it would expose every legacy row to any account that can sign up. Both refusal paths return 403 so the response cannot confirm which producer ids exist. | done — *Correction 2026-11-15: this row said the sibling `GET /store/food-producers/:id/orders/:orderId` "already checked ownership"; it did not (only its PUT did). Closed under SD-64.* |
| ~~D10-2~~ | ~~`proof_pin_code` served on every delivery read.~~ — **fixed 2026-09-10**. The PIN is the secret a recipient reads back to a courier to confirm delivery (`food-deliveries/[id]/route.ts` and `[id]/proof/route.ts` both compare against it), so serializing it defeats the control: anyone holding it can confirm someone else's delivery. It is a credential, not data about the delivery. `modules/food-distribution/public-view.ts` `redactDelivery` strips it at the boundary — applied to the delivery list, the delivery detail, `delivery-batches/:id` and the `active_deliveries` embedded in `couriers/:id` — so it cannot be serialized to *any* caller, authorized or not, independently of how D10-5 is resolved. | done |
| ~~D10-3~~ | ~~`food_order.anonymous_recipient` never read by any path.~~ — **fixed 2026-09-10**. The column has always existed and no read consulted it, so a recipient who asked to be anonymous was returned with their name, phone, email and delivery address anyway. It matters most on `/store/food-donations`, whose rows are donation, gift, community-share, rescue and gleaning orders — food-aid recipients. `applyRecipientAnonymity` now blanks the identity fields and labels the recipient "Anonymous", applied on the donations and food-trades reads. The flag is a promise the schema makes to a person; the read path now keeps it. | done |
| ~~D10-4~~ | ~~`garden_vote.comment_visibility` selected but never applied.~~ — **fixed 2026-09-10**. `GET /store/proposals/:id/votes` selected the column and ignored it, so a comment a voter marked `private` was served to anonymous callers beside their `customer_id`. Only the comment is withheld — the tally still needs every vote, its weight and its voter, and a governance record that quietly dropped ballots would be worse than one showing a comment as withheld. `members_only` is treated as non-public because the route cannot yet tell a member from a stranger; when it can, that case can widen. | done |
| ~~D10-5~~ | ~~**The remaining unauthenticated reads, which need an access-model ruling rather than a patch.**~~ — **ruled and closed 2026-09-13.** The ruling is written once, in `backend/src/shared/community-read-access.ts`, so twelve handlers could not answer it twelve ways. **A `/store/*` read that returns a natural person's identifying, locating, financial or participation data is scoped to someone entitled to it**, in three tiers: the subject or a principal named on the record; a member of the same garden; nobody else. Tier 2 is *membership*, not merely being signed in — an account with no relationship to a garden is a stranger to its roster, and a community garden whose members cannot see each other is broken rather than protected. **Every refusal is 403, and deliberately identical whether the record is missing or merely not the caller's.** Ids here are enumerable — each prefix's own list endpoint supplies them — so a 404 meaning "no such delivery" beside a 403 meaning "not yours" would turn these endpoints into an existence oracle. One code for both says nothing. **Applied to:** `gardens/:id/members` (and `investment_balance` now appears only on the caller's own row — a roster is a member's business, another member's balance is not; `voting_power` stays on all rows because a vote count that only you can see is not a vote count); `work-parties/:id/signups` and `harvests/:id/claims` (both resolve their parent garden and require membership); `volunteer-logs` (400 unless scoped by `garden_id` or `customer_id`, then the subject's own history or a co-member's); `food-deliveries` list, `food-trades` list and `food-donations` (400 unless scoped to a `producer_id`/`courier_id`, then that principal's owner — an unscoped list of everyone's orders is not a query anyone should be able to make); `food-deliveries/:id`, `/:id/track`, `/:id/subscribe` and `food-trades/:id` (producer, courier or recipient); `delivery-batches/:id` (the planner who owns it or the courier driving it). **Two deliberate costs.** A recipient who checked out as a guest has a null `customer_id`, cannot be matched, and loses tracking: giving it back means a per-delivery token on the link, which is a feature to build, not a default to leave open. And ownership lookups use `actorOwnsResource`, not the `actorMayManage` the write verbs use — the latter grandfathers a null `owner_id` so legacy rows stay manageable, which is defensible for a write behind the authenticated prefix matcher and is not defensible for a read of a third party's address. A legacy row is unreadable until an owner is backfilled; the failure is visible to the operator rather than silent to the person whose address is in the payload. Every lookup denies on failure and never throws, so a misconfigured module surfaces as a closed door rather than an open one. Covered by `shared/__tests__/community-read-access.unit.spec.ts` (24) and `api/store/__tests__/d10-5-read-scoping.unit.spec.ts` (23). | done |
| D10-5a | **The courier half of D10-5, closed 2026-09-10 — it needed no ruling.** `GET /store/couriers` and `/store/couriers/:id` served the `food_courier` row verbatim to unauthenticated callers: for people doing gig delivery work, their `email`, `phone`, live `current_latitude`/`_longitude`, `license_plate`, `service_area_center_lat`/`_lng` (usually where they live), `weekly_schedule` (when they are and are not out), `documents`, `background_check_passed` and its date, `total_earnings`, `pending_payout`, `hawala_account_id` — and `emergency_contact_name`/`_phone`, which belong to a third party who never interacted with this platform at all. **Neither reason D10-5 was deferred applied here.** The repository had already declared the public courier field set twice: `/food-deliveries/:id/track` builds `courier: { name, vehicle_type, photo_url }` under the comment "Courier info (public only)", and the model annotates `display_name` as "What customers see". And **nothing consumes either endpoint** — no storefront, no admin or vendor panel, no integration test — so there was no working surface to break. `publicCourierView` is an **allow-list**: a column added to `food_courier` tomorrow is private until someone adds it, since the reverse default is how this row came to publish emergency contacts. Reputation and capability are published (rating, completed deliveries, vehicle, bags, zones, radius) because that is what a courier list is for; the radius goes out without its centre; `verified` goes out but `background_check_passed`, `drivers_license_verified` and `insurance_verified` do not — the platform saying it has checked someone is a different act from republishing that person's screening record. Position is omitted even mid-delivery: the customer that delivery belongs to gets the breadcrumb through `/food-deliveries/:id/track`, which knows who is asking. On the detail route the owner still gets the whole row, keyed on `actorOwnsResource` rather than `actorMayManage` — the latter grandfathers a null `owner_id`, and a courier created before ownership was stamped must not be fully readable by any signed-in account. **`GET /store/delivery-batches/:id` went with it**: unauthenticated, it hand-built `{ id, name: "First Last", phone, vehicle_type }` — more than `/food-deliveries/:id/track` gives even the customer whose delivery is in flight — and now uses the same projection. Who may read a batch at all stays open under D10-5; narrowing the courier neither answers that question nor waits on it. **A dead field turned up alongside it**: `/food-deliveries/:id/track` served `photo_url: courier.photo_url`, and `food_courier` has no `photo_url` column — it has `avatar_url`. The field has been `undefined` on every response since the route shipped, so no customer has ever seen a courier's photo. Now sourced from `avatar_url`, with the response key unchanged (the value was never populated, so nothing can depend on it) and the name taken from `display_name` for consistency with the projection. Touches `backend/src/modules/food-distribution/public-view.ts`, `backend/src/api/store/couriers/route.ts`, `backend/src/api/store/couriers/[id]/route.ts`, `backend/src/api/store/delivery-batches/[id]/route.ts`, `backend/src/api/store/food-deliveries/[id]/track/route.ts`. | done |
| ~~D10-6~~ | ~~`food_producer.hide_address` — declared with the comment "For cottage food / privacy — don't show exact address" and read by no path, so a cottage-food producer working from home has their street address and lat/long published.~~ — **fixed 2026-09-10.** Originally sorted into D10-5's "needs a ruling" bucket, which was wrong: `hide_address` is an *opt-in flag a producer set themselves*, so honouring it is not a guess about audience — it is the same shape as D10-3, and it belonged in the fix-now bucket from the start. `applyProducerAddressPrivacy` nulls `address_line_1/2`, `latitude` and `longitude` on `/store/food-producers` and `/:id`. City, state, postal code and country stay: the flag says *exact* address, and a local food marketplace still has to say roughly where a producer is. Coordinates are nulled rather than rounded — a rounded coordinate still reads as precise to every consumer of the field, and "how coarse is coarse enough" is a judgement nobody has made; a caller needing proximity can use the postal code. `service_area_radius_miles` is kept, since it describes how far someone travels, not where they live. | done |

| ~~D11-1~~ | ~~**The CCPA/CPRA export and deletion endpoints cover a small fraction of the personal data held, while telling the person they cover all of it.**~~ — **closed 2026-09-13.** Found while writing the Privacy Policy, which could not describe the delete button without establishing what it reached: the export returned profile, addresses and orders under a notice claiming it held everything; deletion removed addresses, anonymised the customer record and revoked sign-in. **47 tables carry a `customer_id`** and neither endpoint touched one of them — a past delivery kept the recipient's name, phone and street address, and volunteer attendance, garden membership, ledger balances, governance votes and wellness records all survived a "deletion". **Fixed with one registry, not two longer hand-lists.** `lib/customer-data-registry.ts` names all 47 with a disposition each, and both endpoints consume it, so they cannot describe different sets of data again. The rule behind the dispositions is written down rather than left to be inferred: **`delete`** for a person's own participation record with no third party depending on it; **`anonymise`** where something shared depends on the row but not on the link (a governance vote — removing it silently changes a tally other people relied on); **`retain`** for a completed financial record under a named legal basis, with `basis` required by the type, because a retention without a stated basis is an omission with better grammar. A row that is both a transaction and a bundle of contact details — a food order carrying the delivery address — is `retain` with `anonymiseFields`, so the accounting record survives and the address does not. Wellness records are `delete` outright: an anonymised health record is still a health record about one person. **The part that stops it recurring** is `__tests__/customer-data-registry`, which walks `src/modules/**` and fails the build naming the table and file when a model gains a `customer_id` without an entry — verified by removing an entry and watching it go red, not by a green run. It checks the other direction too, so a stale entry cannot leave the registry describing a system that no longer exists. Erasure runs one statement per entity with per-entity isolation, since a deletion that half-runs and reports nothing is how this started; failures are named in the response and logged, and identifiers are validated before interpolation. `/legal/privacy` §6 still describes the manual escalation route, which remains available. **LEG-2 in `PRE_LAUNCH_AUDIT.md` is closed again**, this time for the whole data set. 17 tests. | done |

| W5-1 | **Patronage `queued → paid` — the disbursement rail, built 2026-09-13.** `patronage-review.ts` stopped at `queued` and said the rest "belongs to a disbursement rail that does not exist yet and whose shape is a Posture A question". **The Posture A answer is narrow: a patronage refund is a vendor payout, so it terminates at Stripe ACH and never at Stellar.** That matters because `dual-rail-selector.ts` exists, picks between `stripe_ach` and `stellar_usdc`, and *prefers Stellar when the bridge is healthy* — correct for the settlements it was written for, and a Posture A violation here. `POSTURE_A_COMPLIANCE.md` is explicit: "No USDC payouts to vendors. Vendor payout always terminates at Stripe ACH to a US bank account." Wiring the selector into this path would have sent a vendor payout over Stellar the moment the bridge came up healthy — arriving by default, with no code change and nothing in a diff to review. The rail is therefore fixed in `patronage-disburse.ts` rather than chosen, with a paragraph saying so, because the next person to see two rails and one payout is the risk. **`planDisbursement` is pure and refuses with reasons** rather than skipping: no payout account, a `hawala`/`manual` provider (neither is Stripe ACH), an account that is `pending`/`restricted`/`suspended`, an active account with no external id, a non-positive amount. **A refusal leaves the row `queued`** — the recoverable state, fix the account and re-run — and `failed` is written only when a payout was attempted and the processor rejected it, so afterwards "we could not send this" and "they would not take it" stay distinguishable. **Money first, status second**, deliberately: the reverse would mark a row paid that never went out, whereas a crash between the two leaves a `queued` row whose payout succeeded — and the idempotency key (`patronage:<period>:<allocation>`, derived from the allocation, not the run) makes the retry a no-op at the processor rather than a second payment. **Dry run is the default.** Without `FBM_PATRONAGE_DISBURSEMENT_LIVE` the endpoint plans and reports and moves nothing, which is the useful half while accounts are still being connected; the flag is named as an assertion about the world, like `FBM_SECURITIES_GATE_CLEARED`. Live with no registered adapter is a 503, not a row marked paid against a rail that is not there. **What remains is operator-side**: registering a `patronageDisbursementPort` adapter that performs the Stripe Connect transfer. The port is a named seam so that adapter is reviewable on its own rather than an API call buried in a route. 24 tests. | done |

**The pattern.** Every one of these is a route whose write verbs were locked
down by the prefix matcher and whose read was not, and the rows split cleanly
into two kinds. D10-2/3/4 needed no decision because the schema *already*
stated the intent — a PIN is a credential, an anonymity flag is a promise, a
visibility enum is a rule — and the read path simply ignored it; those are
bugs. D10-5 and D10-6 were different: the schema says nothing about who may
read, so fixing them meant *choosing* an audience.

Both are now chosen. D10-6 turned out not to need a choice after all — the
producer had already made it by setting `hide_address`. D10-5 did, and the
choice is recorded as prose in `shared/community-read-access.ts` rather than
as twelve independent guards, because the next `/store/*` route that returns
somebody's address will be written by someone who has not read this file. The
rule to apply there: **a read that returns a natural person's identifying,
locating, financial or participation data is scoped, and refuses with 403
whether or not the record exists.** If a genuinely public surface is wanted,
the answer is a projection (`modules/food-distribution/public-view.ts`), not
an open read — a projection narrows *what* is returned, a scope narrows *who*
may ask, and several of these routes want both.

## BM — Black Mask launch, FBM side (2026-10-05)

The FBM steps of `docs/BLACK_MASK_LAUNCH_PLAN.md` §5 the operator has decided.
Each ships behind its own default-off flag; operator answers of 2026-10-05 are
recorded where they decided a design point. The paid launch also waits on L28.

| # | Item | Status | Location |
|---|---|---|---|
| BM-1 | **Consumer subscriptions: four safety fixes now, a renewal charge that can actually collect, and the grace-then-read-only lifecycle the launch spec asks for.** The map found a customer could not buy and be renewed at all: the storefront has no subscription call, the store route never saves a payment method, the live renewal path relies on a provider that forwards neither `off_session` nor a capture, and with `FBM_SUBSCRIPTION_RENEWAL_LIVE` unset (the default, absent from `.env.template`) renewals advance dates and grant entitlements **without charging** — kept byte-identical and recorded here as pre-existing free renewal. **Unconditional fixes:** `POST /store/subscriptions` refuses a cart that is not the signed-in customer's (one `forbidden()` body, nothing created); the subscription detail route answers `forbidden()` for missing and not-owned alike; resume works only from PAUSED and pause only from ACTIVE (re-pausing a non-active row now answers 409 where it used to succeed, needed so cancel-pause-resume cannot reactivate a cancelled row); `failSubscription` merges metadata instead of erasing it; pause and resume drop a stale `paused_reason`. **Live renewal charge** (only with `FBM_SUBSCRIPTION_RENEWAL_LIVE=1`): a direct PaymentIntent on the platform account, off-session, automatic capture, one intent per cycle with its id persisted before confirmation so a retry days later re-confirms the same intent instead of creating a second one (the review found Stripe's 24-hour idempotency window is shorter than the dunning gap — the vendor-plan precedent has the same gap and is left as is); the charge is recorded before the period rolls; a missing payment method goes to dunning, never a free renewal. Verified against the installed SDK only; **a Stripe test-mode run is still required** before go-live, and the Medusa provider key and the vendor-billing key must point at the same account. **Lifecycle** behind new `FF_CONSUMER_SUBSCRIPTIONS_V1`: cancellation or exhausted dunning moves the subscription to `past_due` with a grace end (cancellation keeps access through the paid period plus grace), a sweep moves expired grace to `read_only` (export kept, nothing deleted), and a successful charge during grace restores `active`.
